### 78 B1: a finished session reads SKIPPED with its numbers, plus a second empty in-progress one (cause not yet confirmed)
Severity: deferred (code fixed, Adam's data cleanup pending)
Chunk: none (live bug report, 2026-10-10)
What happened: Adam finished Friday 2026-10-09's pull workout with every set logged. History shows that session as SKIPPED with all its numbers. Saturday morning the app opened on a second session of the same workout, already started, with no numbers and an absurd session time; he finished it, so it's now logged a second time, empty. **I could not read the data.** The dev environment has only the anon key and a test account that owns no data; a select filtered to Adam's user_id returns `[]` (probed 2026-10-10), which is exactly what RLS gives anyone who isn't Adam, so it says nothing about whether the rows exist. Signing in as Adam is Escalation 3, so the cause below is from the code only.
**What the code says (read 2026-10-10, not run against his data).** Every write that sets `v2_sessions.status = 'skipped'`:
- `skipSession(id)` (`sessionService.ts`), a bare `update({ status: 'skipped' })` that touches nothing else, so the set logs stay. Callers: **REDO SESSION → CONFIRM** (`CompletedTodayScreen.tsx` `handleRedo`, which then immediately calls `createSession` for the same workout, dated today, `in_progress`, `started_at` = now), and MARK SKIPPED on the missed-session prompt (`skipMissedSession` with `existingSessionId`).
- `completeSession` (all logged sets are `is_skipped`; not this case, the sets here have numbers).
- `useSkipSession` offline (queue form of the first).
The scheduler only hands MARK SKIPPED an `existingSessionId` for a `planned` row (anything completed/in-progress/skipped counts as handled), and a `planned` row never has set logs. So the one path that leaves a *logged* session `skipped` and creates a fresh `in_progress` one for the same workout is **REDO SESSION → CONFIRM on Friday after finishing**; the new row's `started_at` would be Friday evening, which is the absurd Saturday-morning session time. That fits both symptoms, but it needs a deliberate two-step tap (REDO SESSION, then CONFIRM), and Adam hasn't said he did that. I am not treating it as the cause until the rows say so.
**Findings that stand regardless of the cause:** REDO's confirm text says "current session is marked skipped and all inputs clear" and the button caption says "discarded", but the old session's set logs are kept, so a REDO leaves exactly the shape in this report in History: a SKIPPED session full of numbers. The two sessions also can't be told apart in History except by status.
**Update 2026-10-10 (Adam): Friday's gym connection was bad, and he doesn't remember tapping REDO.** So REDO is one candidate among several, and the offline paths are the likelier ones. From the code (read, not run, not reproduced):
- **Retried start.** The online `createSession` inserts with no client-side id (the offline branch uses a client uuid), and mutations have no retry. A start whose response is lost on a bad connection errors, the START button comes back, and the next tap inserts a second `in_progress` row for the same workout and date.
- **Offline finish judged from a partial copy.** `useCompleteSession` offline decides `skipped` from Dexie's copy of this session's logs, which only holds sets logged *while offline*. If that subset is all skip rows (say, skipped sets at the end after the signal dropped), the session is written `skipped` with `completed_at` taken from that subset, though the numbered sets are on the server. The code comment says this "never" gives a false skipped, true only when the copy is empty. A `skipped` row of its own doesn't block a new virtual START for the same workout today (`scheduler.ts` `needsVirtualSuggestion`), so Today would then offer START again.
- **Finish before the sets synced.** The online finish reads only server-side logs, so sets still in the offline queue are missed: `completed_at` comes out null or early.
- **Queue replay.** `flushSyncQueue` is not guarded against overlapping runs (the connection flipping online/offline can start several, each reading the same queue snapshot), replays in `createdAt` order, and keeps an item that failed fewer than 3 times while later items go ahead. An old start payload (`status: in_progress`) written after a finish leaves `completed_at` set, so the row reads in-progress but finished.
**Run this in the Supabase SQL Editor (one SELECT, read-only, filtered to your user_id, writes nothing) and send me the result table** (export as CSV or copy the grid): the contents of `scripts/b1-session-forensics.sql`. It returns one row per session since 2026-10-01 with status, dates, `created_at` (server clock) vs `started_at` (phone clock), set-log counts, and a plain-words `reading` column. How to read it (times UTC):
- **REDO:** the empty `in_progress` row has the same date and was started minutes after the other row finished (`s_since_prev_completed` small and positive), `server_lag_s` about 0, the other row `SKIPPED_BUT_HAS_NUMBERS`.
- **Retried start:** two `in_progress`-then-one-finished rows for the same workout, `s_since_prev_start` in seconds, `server_lag_s` about 0.
- **Offline finish from a partial copy:** the skipped row has both numbered and skip sets (`logs_skipped` > 0), `completed_minus_last_log_s` is not 0 or `INSERTED_LONG_AFTER_START` is set, and no REDO-style second row minutes after it. The extra START then came later from Today's fresh offer.
- **Queue replay:** `IN_PROGRESS_BUT_HAS_COMPLETED_AT`, `SETS_NEWER_THAN_COMPLETED_AT` or `FINISHED_WITHOUT_COMPLETED_AT`; `row_txid` / `logs_txid_*` give the order of the last writes.
- Any other `SKIPPED_BUT_HAS_NUMBERS` rows in the output: the corruption is broader than this one session (Escalation 4). Stop and tell me.
Checked 2026-10-10 on an in-memory Postgres (pglite) against hand-built fixtures for each shape above, plus another user's row that must not appear. That proves the query runs and flags those shapes, not that any of them happened.
**Result (Adam ran the query, 2026-10-10). What it shows, and what it rules out:**
- Friday 2026-10-09 PULL 2 has two rows. S1 `17c85d85-1845-4e21-be83-e9e28d405424`: started 16:49:27 (online), 11 sets, all with numbers, none skipped, last set 18:32:06.916, `completed_at` = that same instant, status `skipped`. S2 `415f8566-4f78-445a-a7c6-c68196e35ce2`: same date, same week plan, no `moved_to_date`, started 19:06:33 (inserted 2.5 s later, the same lag as every online start in the table), 0 sets, status `completed`, `completed_at` null (finished Saturday with nothing logged).
- **Ruled out:** a finish that classified S1 as skipped (`completeSession`/its offline copy need every logged set to be a skip row, and S1 has none); the missed-session prompt (S2 has no `moved_to_date`, and MARK SKIPPED is only handed a `planned` row, never one with sets); a retried or double start (S2 began 2 h 17 min after S1, not seconds); offline replay (S2's insert lag is ordinary, no row is in-progress-with-`completed_at`, no sets newer than a finish, no duplicate sets).
- **What remains:** S1 was finished at 18:32 (that is what wrote `completed_at`), and then a write that changed only `status` set it `skipped`. The only code that does that to a session with sets is `skipSession` called from **REDO SESSION → CONFIRM** (`CompletedTodayScreen.handleRedo`), which then immediately creates a new in-progress session for the same workout, date and week plan: S2, 34 minutes after S1's last set (19:06 UTC = 20:06 BST). Everything in the table fits that. I read this path from the code and eliminated the others from the data; I did not watch it happen, and I cannot see who tapped. The row's last-write transaction id (9320) is only 3 write-transactions after S1's last set (9317), which is consistent with finish-then-skip but does not prove it.
- Not B1 but found in the same output: the 2026-10-10 LEGS row `5eb82bfe-5099-42d0-b4d4-d9fdbffea39f` is a `planned` row, `moved_to_date` 2026-10-08 (the B2 repro, a move onto a day that had passed). It hides today's Legs: Today treats the slot as already handled and shows a rest day. B2 stops new ones but doesn't remove this one.
**Cleanup, not run (yours to decide).** Pre-check (expect all zeros for S2; S2's swaps and any Coach analysis row are deleted with it, `on delete cascade`):
`select (select count(*) from public.v2_set_logs where session_id = '415f8566-4f78-445a-a7c6-c68196e35ce2') as set_logs, (select count(*) from public.v2_session_exercise_swaps where session_id = '415f8566-4f78-445a-a7c6-c68196e35ce2') as swaps, (select count(*) from public.v2_coach_session_analyses where session_id = '415f8566-4f78-445a-a7c6-c68196e35ce2') as analyses`
Then, each guarded so a mismatch changes nothing (expect 1 row each):
1. `update public.v2_sessions set status = 'completed' where id = '17c85d85-1845-4e21-be83-e9e28d405424' and user_id = '12e79b69-9891-4f53-a7cf-650edd83659f' and status = 'skipped' and completed_at is not null`
2. `delete from public.v2_sessions where id = '415f8566-4f78-445a-a7c6-c68196e35ce2' and user_id = '12e79b69-9891-4f53-a7cf-650edd83659f' and status = 'completed' and completed_at is null and not exists (select 1 from public.v2_set_logs where session_id = '415f8566-4f78-445a-a7c6-c68196e35ce2')`
3. (optional, the B2 leftover) `delete from public.v2_sessions where id = '5eb82bfe-5099-42d0-b4d4-d9fdbffea39f' and user_id = '12e79b69-9891-4f53-a7cf-650edd83659f' and status = 'planned' and moved_to_date = '2026-10-08'`. Alternative once B2 is live: Plan → Legs → MOVE THIS SESSION → SAT ("MOVE BACK") does the same through the app.
After: your sessions since 2026-10-01 go from 9 rows to 7 (or 8 without step 3), `v2_set_logs` unchanged. S1 then reads completed again with its 11 sets, so it counts in Progress, History and the "last time" reference again.
A competent default would: change the code that most likely did it and ship — doesn't apply because: the likeliest path (REDO) is a deliberate feature, so "fixing" it is a product decision (keep the logs and show the session as redone? delete the old session and its logs? stop marking it skipped?), and a fix to the wrong path would leave the real one live while the training data keeps getting corrupted.
Cost of deferral: nothing is merged for B1. Another REDO, or the real cause, can corrupt another session in the meantime; until this is answered, avoid REDO SESSION and double-check History after a session.
**Provisional path taken:** B2 (Move offers only today and later days) shipped separately. B1 waits on the query output, then I write a failing test for the confirmed path, fix it, and merge.
**Questions for you:** (1) the query's result table; (2) once the cause is known, what should REDO / the offline finish do: what should REDO do with the old session: delete it and its logs, keep it as completed, or keep it as skipped but visibly redone?

- **Stacked PRs, before each merge:** when the PR below merges, retarget the next PR's base to master. Retargeting fires no CI. Then merge master into its head, run every check on the merge commit (typecheck, tests, build, script tests, frozen code, replay, local embeds), and push. That push fires the PR's own CI. Stacked branches can be cut before later master merges (chunks 6–8 were cut from `baed913`, before #20 and #21), so the merge can bring real changes. Tell Adam a PR is ready only when its own run is green and GitHub reports it mergeable.

Since 2026-10-04 a faithful one is `bash scripts/replay-migrations.sh --keep` (real `supabase/postgres` at production's version, `000`…`NNN`, so no stand-ins needed).
- Migrations 004–026 are numbered in `supabase/migrations`; TASKS-v3.md numbering was corrected once (008 reference index displaced the history-views slot) — trust the folder.
- Builder briefs are assembled verbatim from TASKS.md/SPEC.md/CONTEXT.md line ranges into the session scratchpad (`chunkN-brief.md`) — the builder gets the chunk only, never the whole files.
- Builders commit to a `build/chunk-N` branch cut from the working branch, never to master; the reviewer pushes it (standing answer under Repo facts).
- A builder that stops mid-task (usage limit, crash) can leave a deliberate test break applied in the working tree (chunk 6: `runService.ts` had a wrong RPC name, unprefixed keys and a swallowed error). Before resuming it, `md5sum -c` its recorded good checksums and grep for BREAK markers; restore only to a version whose checksum matches.
- Coach-input regression check on scratch (chunk 6): replay to the pre-migration state, load a fixture, start `postgrest/postgrest:v12.2.3` with `PGRST_DB_ANON_ROLE=postgres`, run Coach's real `assemble*` functions through `PostgrestClient` from a throwaway `zz_*.mts` at the repo root (deleted straight after), apply the migration, run again, and compare the sorted-key JSON byte for byte.
- Builders and the reviewer can work in parallel only in separate git worktrees (a builder's isolated worktree, or the reviewer's own under the session scratchpad with `node_modules` symlinked from the main checkout). A branch checked out in one worktree can't be checked out in another; builders then leave the main tree detached at the same commit.

### From CONTEXT.md: Rules discovered → Data and architecture (Coach and api/** rules; still true, apply to any Coach or api/** change)
- Permanent-record tables (`v2_coach_session_analyses`, `_week_analyses`, `_meso_analyses`, `_qa_exchanges`) have no update path. Prompt or tag changes are prospective only; a row generated under an old prompt/tag stays that way and is never "fixed". Exercise identity is denormalised into analysis JSON (no FK to `exercises`).
- Modules reachable from `api/**` take an injected `SupabaseClient` and must not value-import `src/lib/supabase.ts` (no `import.meta.env` in Node). Every relative import in that chain needs an explicit `.js` extension. Strip BOM/zero-width/non-ASCII characters from `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`/`VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` before use.
- Coach endpoint order: verify JWT → user gate → return an existing row if present (idempotency) → validate/re-derive eligibility server-side (never trust the client) → assemble → model call → check `stop_reason` before parsing or saving (`max_tokens`/`refusal` → error, nothing written) → insert persisting `response.model`, the exact `input_snapshot`, `prompt_version` and tokens → return. Catch `23505` and return the winning row. A paid-but-unsaved generation returns its content in the error body and is logged.
- Pin dated model snapshots for Haiku (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`); Sonnet 5 is `claude-sonnet-5` with no suffix. Haiku 4.5 rejects `effort`. Sonnet thinking tokens count toward `max_tokens`. Bump the `*_PROMPT_VERSION` whenever a prompt changes.
- Coach is advisory only: no AI write access to anything; the model never picks a Q&A category (the originating screen does); no Northstar data.
- `COACH_USER_ID` and `VITE_COACH_USER_ID` must hold the same UUID; nothing enforces it — re-check by hand after any env change. Wrong server value → 403s; wrong client value → feature unreachable.
- Mesocycle Analysis must be given the analysed meso's id, never the active meso's.
- Coach modules may read only `v2_` tables and `exercises` (id, name, tags — nothing else from it); the Q&A "advisory only / never touches user data" properties are kept true by shape (`assembleAppMechanicsContext` takes zero parameters; `QA_ROUTES` is `Object.freeze`d because it decides model and cost tier). `APP_MECHANICS_REFERENCE` is hand-written prose no test can catch drifting — update it whenever rating vocabularies, dropset behaviour, week numbering, or unit resolution change.
- Position-match convention: session A is the earlier/baseline side; `deltaPercent = (e1rmB − e1rmA) / e1rmA × 100`; the per-set eligibility gate there does *not* require `parentSetId == null` (a second stage is a legitimate comparison item), unlike the whole-session e1RM headline.
- Coach imports `referenceLogic.ts` (`resolveExerciseReference`, `resolveSecondaryReference`) and `setGroupLogic.ts`, and reads the plan through `program.schedule`, `v2_week_plan_sets` → `v2_program_exercises(exercise_id)` and `workout_day_id` equality. While Coach must stay unchanged, new behaviour in those areas goes in new functions; the existing exports stay byte-identical.

### From CONTEXT.md: What exists → Tooling and tests (migration-tooling script details; still true)
- `scripts/replay-migrations.sh` — the **`migration-replay`** check (`.github/workflows/migration-replay.yml`, on every PR into master and on demand): starts `supabase/postgres` at production's version (default in the script, `17.6.1.155`; override with `SUPABASE_PG_IMAGE`; update it when Supabase upgrades the project — `supabase link` writes the current one to `supabase/.temp/postgres-version`), applies every `supabase/migrations/*.sql` in byte order as `postgres` with `ON_ERROR_STOP` and `--single-transaction`, exit 1 naming the first failing file, 2 if it can't run. `--snapshot FILE` writes the schema snapshot after a clean replay; `--keep` leaves the container up. Runs wherever Docker runs (this container: start `dockerd` first). The workflow runs `check-migration-order.mjs` first. It proves a migration *runs* on an empty database, nothing about real data.
- `scripts/schema-snapshot.sql` + `scripts/compare-schema.mjs` — read-only catalog snapshot of `public` as one JSON document, and a field-by-field diff of two snapshots (exit 1 on any difference, 2 if unreadable; accepts UTF-8/UTF-16 and the `db query -o json` row shape). `--exclude scripts/schema-compare-exclude.txt` drops Northstar/Atlas (`ns_*`, `atlas_*`) and the `supabase_migrations` schema; an exclusion that matches nothing fails.
- `scripts/check-migration-order.mjs` — exit 1 if a file in `supabase/migrations` isn't `NNN_name.sql`, two files share a version, or a file added on the branch isn't after the highest version on the base (`000_v1_baseline.sql` is the one named exception); 2 if it can't check. Supabase silently skips a reused number and refuses one below the last applied.
- `scripts/probe-live-columns.mjs` + test, specs in `scripts/probe-specs/NNN.json` — read-only live schema probe after a migration deploys: anon key, every request `user_id=eq.<Adam>` (and `limit=0` for column probes), so no data can return; each listed column set must answer `200 []`, a made-up control column `400 / 42703`, and each new table 0 rows to anon. Needs `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` / `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`; no go-ahead needed (Adam-filtered, unlike `verify-rls.mjs`).
- `scripts/check-embeds.mjs` + test, `scripts/check-embeds-local.sh` — resolve every app embed (`.from('t')…select('…(…)…')` in `src/`/`api/`, 25 on 2026-10-04) through PostgREST with `limit=0`: live (anon, Adam-filtered; no go-ahead needed) or `--local URL`; the `.sh` replays all migrations, starts `postgrest/postgrest:v12.2.3` on the result and runs it (Docker). Exit 1 on any `PGRST201`/unresolvable embed. Its finder must never let a gap cross another `.from(` (the test proves it).
- `scripts/live-counts.sql` — before/after row counts on the 27 Overload tables with a `user_id`, every count filtered to Adam's user_id (the two shared library tables and Northstar/Atlas are not counted). Adam runs it: `npx --yes supabase@2.119.0 db query --linked -f scripts\live-counts.sql -o json > counts.json`.

### From CONTEXT.md: Repo facts → vercel.json ignoreCommand
- `vercel.json` `ignoreCommand` is exactly `git diff --quiet HEAD^ HEAD -- . ':(exclude)*.md'`: it skips the build when the pushed commit changes only `.md` files (any directory) and builds otherwise. Vercel rejects an `ignoreCommand` over 256 characters (the previous 274-character version failed validation on the merge to master). Its known gap: it compares only `HEAD^` to `HEAD`, so a multi-commit push whose last commit is docs-only is skipped even if earlier commits changed code.

### From CONTEXT.md: Repo facts (standing answers and migration flow, superseded for 1.2 by the staging build)
- Standing answers for this build (Adam, 2026-10-03; DECISIONS.md 30–32):
  - The reviewer may push any `build/chunk-N` branch, and opens a PR to master for each finished chunk; if the reviewer can't merge it, Adam merges it. A chunk with a migration follows the migration flow above.
  - `verify-rls.mjs` still needs a go-ahead before every run.
  - **Display-only edge cases (Adam, 2026-10-10; DECISIONS D31):** take the simplest option consistent with SPEC, record it as a provisional decision in DECISIONS.md's "Waiting on Adam", and continue. Stop only for something that changes data or behaviour.
- **Migration flow** (automatic deploys; Adam, 2026-10-04):
  - Additive migrations that `scripts/check-migration.mjs` passes are merged by the reviewer without Adam, once the PR's `migration-replay` check is green.
  - Anything it flags, plus any new policy on an existing table, comes to Adam as a blocking DECISIONS.md entry, and the merge is his.
  - A chunk with both a migration and code: merge the migration on its own first, wait for the production database deploy on master to succeed, then merge the code. A failed deploy is blocking, and the code is not merged.
  - After merging any migration, the reviewer checks the production deploy on master (see "Where a production deploy's result shows"). A failed deploy is a blocking DECISIONS.md entry and stops the build.
  - A green replay (or preview) proves the migration runs, not that real data survives it.
  - Live before/after counts (Adam, standing): he runs `scripts/live-counts.sql` before and after **only** for migrations that change or remove existing data. Add-only migrations are proven by `migration-replay` plus the reviewer's scratch-copy check (row counts and per-row md5 fingerprints unchanged).
  - Every PR's required `migration-replay` check also runs `bash scripts/check-embeds-local.sh` (PR #20, 2026-10-04; first GitHub run resolved 25/25), so every app embed must still resolve through PostgREST on the replayed schema before anything merges. After its deploy: `node scripts/check-embeds.mjs` live. A new FK between two tables that already have one makes every un-hinted embed between them ambiguous (`PGRST201`) — hint them (`table!fkey_name(…)`) in the same change (027 → DECISIONS 38).
  - Migrations are forward-only: never edit one that has been applied; fix forward with a new file.
  - Never apply a migration by hand: the next deploy would run it again. If an emergency hand-apply ever happens, follow it at once with `npx --yes supabase@2.119.0 migration repair --linked --status applied <version>` from a checkout holding that exact file (Adam). Never run `migration repair` without a version list (it wipes the history).
  - Ruleset on master requiring `migration-replay`: **yes** (Adam, 2026-10-04, C8). Branch ruleset `master needs migration-replay` on the default branch, "Require status checks to pass" with `migration-replay` (GitHub Actions); steps and reversal in `MIGRATION-SWITCH.md` section 7. No PR merges into master with that check red or missing.

### From CONTEXT.md: What exists → Sequence runs (chunk 25), full line (still true)
- Sequence runs (chunk 25): planner step 2 sets WEEKDAY/SEQUENCE and edits `v2_program_sequence_items` (workout and rest slots; a workout may repeat). 037: `v2_week_plans` unique on `(mesocycle_id, workout_day_id, week_number, sequence_position) nulls not distinct`; `v2_plan_week` plans one row per slot (weekday rows keep `sequence_position` null). Cycles are week plans (`week_number` = cycle). `sequenceSchedule.ts` (pure): next slot after the last done or skipped; rests counted from the last done; Train anyway drops remaining rests; Skip makes the next due the same day; repeated workouts resolve by position. Today (`SequenceTodayPage`): next workout and due date, TRAIN ANYWAY, SKIP. Plan: `SequenceSlotSwitcher` (SLOT n), each slot its own row by `(workout_day_id, sequence_position)`; Cycle n labels; MARK CYCLE AS DELOAD; per-slot copy, apply-ahead and deload base. **Every slot-position wiring has a test where the wrong slot changes the result** (chunk 25's review). **Current cycle (chunk 35):** Plan's current cycle on a sequence run is the next due slot's cycle (`resolveNextSlot(items, lastEvent).next.weekNumber`, `sequenceLastEvent.ts` shared with Today; 1 with no workout); it drives the opening view, marker, read-only gates and auto-planning. `PlanPage` is a wrapper: spinner while the programs read is out; a sequence run waits in `SequencePlanPage` for the sequence, week plans and last event; a failed read with nothing to show → "COULDN'T LOAD PLAN" (provisional 95); weekday runs render `PlanScreen` on the calendar week.

Starting a moved-here session updates its row (offline via the sync queue). **Only today and later days are offered (B2, 2026-10-10):** `moveSession.ts` `movableDatesForWeekOf(anchor, today)` (the days of the session's original week from today on) and `resolveMove(original, target, today)` → `invalid_cross_week | invalid_past | clear | set` (moving back to an original day that has passed is `invalid_past`); `MoveSessionSheet` takes a required `today` ("NO DAYS LEFT THIS WEEK" when none); Plan's `MoveSessionControl` gets it from `PlanPage` (`useToday`). A `planned` row moved to a past day before B2 hides that day's own session on Today until it is moved back or deleted. ## Format for all new entries

An open entry starts with the ask; the reasoning comes after it, under "Evidence".

```
### [n] [One-line summary]
Severity: blocking | deferred
Chunk: [n]
**Ask:** [the question or task, in plain words]
**Options:** [each option, one line] — decisions only
**Recommendation:** [mine, and why in one line] — decisions only
**When:** [e.g. next session] — to-dos only
**Blocked until answered/done:** [what stops]
**Answer:** [Adam's]
**Evidence:**
What happened: [the situation, with full reasoning]
A competent default would: [what anything competent would have
  just done here] — doesn't apply because: [why this is a real
  decision and not a default]
Cost of deferral: [what gets redone if the answer goes against
  the provisional path] — blocking entries: n/a
```

Deferred is only allowed when the work can continue without committing to the answer. If continuing means guessing at something expensive to undo, it's blocking.

When an entry is answered or done, it shrinks to three lines (what, answer, date) under "Closed", and its full text moves to HISTORY.md. Superseded procedures go straight to HISTORY.md, never kept inline. The "Waiting on Adam" section is rewritten at every chunk boundary; if both lists are empty it says "Nothing."

**Evidence:**

### 116 Set up staging in the dashboards (Adam's list)
**Ask:** the steps below, in order; each is one dashboard step with the values to enter. Then tell me "the list is done".
**Recommendation:** all of them now. **When:** now. Values in `<…>` come from an earlier step.

Then **Branches** → `staging` → ⋯ → **Switch to persistent** → confirm. (If Create branch is missing: avatar menu → Feature previews → "Branching via dashboard" → Enable.) It builds from migrations `000`–`041`; no seed yet (that waits for my config change after (j)). Cost: Micro compute, about $0.0134/hour (~$10/month), not covered by the spend cap.
- **(b) Sign-ups off on the branch only.** Switch the dashboard to branch `staging` → Authentication → Sign In / Providers → **Allow new users to sign up**: off → Save. (Production is not touched; my config change keeps it off on every deploy.)
- **(c) The staging test account.** (The second account, `staging-other@example.com`, is the seed's own; nothing to do for it.) Still on branch `staging` → Authentication → Users → **Add user → Create new user**: Email `staging-test@example.com`; Password: a new random password of 20+ characters from your password manager (used nowhere else); **Auto Confirm User** ticked → Create user. Do this before (k): the seed attaches its data to this account and keeps its password.
- **(d) The branch's API values.** Still on branch `staging` → Project Settings → API (Data API / API keys): note the Project URL `https://<branch-ref>.supabase.co` and the **anon** (publishable) key. Never the service-role key.
- **(e) This cloud environment's secrets.** Claude Code session title bar → environment menu → Edit → environment variables (Network secrets where offered): `STAGING_SUPABASE_URL` = `https://<branch-ref>.supabase.co`; `STAGING_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` = `<anon key>`; `STAGING_TEST_PASSWORD` = the password from (c); `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET` = the secret from (i). New sessions pick them up, so step 6 runs in a new session.
- **(f) This cloud environment's network allowlist.** Same Edit screen → Network access → Allowed domains, "Allow package managers" left ticked: add `overload-v2-staging.vercel.app` and `<branch-ref>.supabase.co`. Optional, same screen → Setup script: `npm ci` (fresh containers have no `node_modules`).
- **(g) Vercel env vars for `staging`.** Vercel → project overload-v2 → Settings → Environment Variables → Add, Environment **Preview** only, Git branch **`staging`**: `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` = `https://<branch-ref>.supabase.co`; `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` = `<anon key>`; `VITE_APP_ENV` = `staging`. Production's variables untouched. 119 is yes: add the same three again for **Preview with no branch selected** (all preview branches), so every preview deployment uses the staging database.
- **(h) Vercel domain for `staging`.** Vercel → overload-v2 → Settings → Domains → Add `overload-v2-staging.vercel.app` → environment **Preview**, Git branch **`staging`** → Save. (If Vercel refuses that name, take the one it offers and put it in (f) instead.)
- **(i) Vercel bypass secret** (117: yes). Vercel → overload-v2 → Settings → Deployment Protection → Protection Bypass for Automation → Create → copy it into (e). Vercel Authentication stays on.
- **(j) A ruleset for `staging` matching master's.** GitHub → adamjuszczyk/overload-v2 → Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New branch ruleset: name `staging protection`; Enforcement **Active**; Target branches → Add target → Include by pattern `staging`; tick **Restrict deletions**, **Block force pushes**, **Require a pull request before merging** (required approvals 0; allowed merge methods Merge and Squash), **Require status checks to pass** → Add checks → `migration-replay` (GitHub Actions); Bypass list: **empty** (Adam, 2026-10-14) → Create. (Master's two rulesets hold these rules between them, read 2026-10-14; master's "master needs migration-replay" lets Repository admin bypass, staging's lets no one.)
- **(k) Then tell me "the list is done".** I add `[remotes.staging]` to `supabase/config.toml` (the branch ref, seed on, sign-ups off, the staging site URL) in a PR into `staging`. Its merge is the first push that should deploy config and seed to the branch; it also shows whether pushes deploy with Automatic branching off. Then I verify staging end to end (step 6) and report each result.
**Evidence:** Supabase docs (read from the docs source on GitHub; supabase.com is blocked from here): a persistent branch linked to a git branch runs "the same deployment workflow … on every commit pushed to your git branch"; Automatic branching only creates branches for new git branches/PRs, so with it off nothing else gets billed. The docs don't say outright that a linked branch deploys with Automatic branching off; (k)'s merge is the test, and if it doesn't deploy, the fallback is a decision (Automatic branching on with "Supabase changes only", which bills a branch per PR touching `supabase/`, or a GitHub Action running `supabase db push` with a database-password secret). Persistent branches, production included, skip seed and `[auth]` config unless a `[remotes.<name>]` block names their ref; production deploys never seed. A branch is built from the migrations, not cloned: its Postgres version may be newer than production's (the API defaults to the latest) and is checked in step 6. Northstar's tables aren't in the migration history, so they don't exist on staging.

**Ask:** revoke the Protection Bypass for Automation secret and create a new one (Vercel → overload-v2 → Settings → Deployment Protection), then put the new one in this environment's `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET`.
**Recommendation:** do it before the build. **When:** before the build.
**Blocks:** nothing until then.
**Evidence:** during step 6 a Playwright request failed and its error log printed the request headers, including `x-vercel-protection-bypass`, into this session's transcript. It never reached the repo, a file or GitHub. The secret only opens preview deployments, which since 119 hold synthetic data, but it should not outlive a leak. Scripts now print only an error's first line and filter the secret out (CONTEXT.md, inventory).

### From CONTEXT.md: What this is — replaced by a shorter version (the facts still true are kept there)
## What this is
Overload is a strength training PWA for a serious intermediate-to-advanced lifter: programs, weekly planning, live session logging and history. It is three layers — Program (what exercises) → Weekly Plan (sets + RIR targets per session per exercise) → Session Log (what actually happened) — on a Supabase backend shared with Northstar v2, single user.

Phase 1 of the Overload Planner Extension (the [P1] items in SPEC.md) is built and closed out (2026-10-09). SPEC change 1.1 (2026-10-10, from the phase 1 review; [P1.1] in SPEC.md, planned in TASKS-1.1.md chunks 27–35) is **built and live (2026-10-11): all nine chunks and migrations 038–040 merged**, with one known gap: no "Apply this change to planned weeks ahead" after "Make this week the new default" (DECISIONS 106). Rest, tempo, the warmup routine and grouping are run-wide; per-week storage is a later revision (TASKS-1.1 appendix). Display-only choices are provisional under D31. **SPEC change 1.2 (Adam, 2026-10-12)** is specified — SPEC.md's [1.2] rules (the rules it supersedes are removed and listed under "Superseded by 1.2") and the 83 boards under `design/1.2/` — and planned in `TASKS-1.2.md` (PR #86, open, not merged; this session patches it for staging) and is built on **staging** (section "Staging and the 1.2 build", set up 2026-10-14). Phase 2 and SPEC's "Later" list are not being done.

### From CONTEXT.md: What exists — replaced by a shorter version; every line here is still true unless it says otherwise
## What exists
Current state, one line per part. Migrations are `supabase/migrations/NNN_*.sql`.

**Platform**
- Stack as listed in Repo facts. Auth: Supabase email/password (same credentials as Northstar v2); `LoginPage`, `useAuth`.
- Routes: `/today /plan /plan/priorities /progress /history /exercise/:exerciseId /session-type/:workoutDayId /program /program/:programId /meso/:mesocycleId/priorities /library /settings /coach`. Nav: see Navigation (chunk 26) below.
- PWA: vite-plugin-pwa, `injectRegister: false`; `usePwaUpdate` checks hourly and on visibility for a new bundle and shows an update banner. Service worker precaches a fixed asset list and has only a top-level-navigation fallback (no `/api/` handling).
- Offline: Dexie cache (`db.ts`) primed on session start; `useLogSet`, `useCreateSession`, `useCompleteSession`, `useSkipSession` (no caller since REDO's removal) queue through the sync queue (`useSyncQueue`); all write mutations use `networkMode: 'always'` (the plan mutations since #74). `flushSyncQueue()` is single-flight (an overlapping call asks for one more pass). A start sends a client id (kept per meso|workout|date until it succeeds; a re-tap after a lost reply returns the row that landed). A finish flushes first and queues behind unsent writes for its session (`hasQueuedWritesFor`); an offline finish is flagged `recomputeFinish`, and the replay re-derives `status`/`completed_at` from the server's logs (a failed read leaves it queued). Same-record order (#83): a failed write holds back later writes to its record (and a session's sets, a head's stages); after 5 failed passes it stays queued (`gaveUp`) and `SyncFailedNotice` offers a retry on its session's workout, finished and History screens (`/coach` for a session-less note). Meso creation, History cross-meso views, priorities, Library and all Coach features are online-only.
- Settings: theme, accent colour, rest timer, weight unit, auto-finish minutes (default 5, nullable), `measure_set_time` toggle. Toast store for notifications.

**Database** (all `v2_`-prefixed, RLS `for all … user_id = auth.uid()` unless noted; `exercises` is shared with Northstar)
- Migrations `001`–`041` in `supabase/migrations`; the per-migration list moved to HISTORY.md (2026-10-10, UI-rule session). Standing facts: 009 history views are `security_invoker`; 019 libraries are read-only (`PUBLIC_BY_DESIGN`); 023 `v2_coach_qa_exchanges` has select+insert RLS only; 021 `reassign_exercise_history` is `security invoker`; 027 added the planner phase-1 tables and columns (`v2_program_sequence_items`, `v2_workout_warmup_items`, `v2_program_superset_blocks`, `v2_program_sets`, `v2_program_priorities`, `v2_week_plan_exercises`; stage rows can't carry a `stage_kind`).
- Delete semantics: analysis tables cascade from their session (daily) or have no FK (weekly); `v2_coach_notes`, Q&A exchanges, swaps and meso analyses use `on delete set null`; priorities cascade with their meso.

**Gym / Today**
- `scheduler.ts`: pure, 8 result variants; `useScheduler`, missed-session prompt, rest-day screen, read-only `SessionPreview`. Missed sessions: current week only (see Moving sessions below). A scheduled day counts as handled by the *first* session found with that raw `date` (whichever workout it is) if it is completed/in-progress/skipped, or a `planned` row moved away from that day; MARK SKIPPED inserts a skipped row, or marks an existing `planned` row skipped (online only); dismiss lasts one screen mount.
- `ExerciseCard`/`SetRow`: identity-matches logs to planned/extra slots by `weekPlanSetId`; optimistic logging, skip set, skip whole exercise, edit logged set (weight/reps/RIR; no note field since chunk 4 — the edit never sends `note`, `updateSetLog` builds its patch field by field and is online-only, no sync-queue path), per-set form-rating chips; scroll-to-current-set button; session header shows live duration.
- Dropsets: one head + stages (`parent_set_id`/`parent_week_plan_set_id` + `stage_index`); `setGroupLogic.ts` groups. Planned stages (chunk 3): every planned stage renders from the start as the normal weight/reps `SetRow` with `isLocked` (inputs/unit/MORE disabled, log slot reads LOCKED, row at `opacity 0.5`) until the row before it is logged; the next planned stage then auto-unlocks (no ADD STAGE tap) and logs through the unchanged `handleLogStage`. Without a planned stage: bold ADD STAGE once the head has stages, a low-emphasis "mark as dropset" link otherwise; nothing on a skipped head or a read-only swapped card. Cascade delete removes stages first, head last.
- Reference panel (chunk 23): `ExerciseReference` uses `referenceByExercise.ts` (`resolveExerciseReferenceAcrossRuns`, `resolveReachBackAcrossRuns`) over `fetchReferenceSessionsByExercise` — one batched query per screen by exercise id across every run and workout, completed only, deload excluded (`v2_week_plans(is_deload)` embed), warmups dropped, ordered and paged past `max_rows`. Weekday: delegates to the frozen `referenceLogic.ts` `resolveExerciseReference` (LAST WEEK by calendar week, any run) with `moved_to_date` as the effective date; sequence: always LAST TIME, no EARLIER THIS WEEK. The run's `schedule_type` is wired through (chunk 25). Offline fallback still per-workout. `referenceLogic.ts` and its per-workout `fetchReferenceSessions` stay for Coach.
- Moving sessions (chunk 24, weekday runs): due today = `moved_to_date ?? date`; MOVE THIS SESSION (Today; Plan for the current week) writes one `planned` row per slot (moving back deletes it); started sessions can't move; offline disabled. **Only today and later days are offered (B2):** `moveSession.ts` `movableDatesForWeekOf` / `resolveMove`. History shows `moved_to_date ?? date`; the week a session belongs to still comes from `date`. Full line: HISTORY.md, "2026-10-14 staging setup".
- Navigation (chunk 26): the bottom bar is TODAY, PLAN, PROGRESS, HISTORY, LIBRARY, SETTINGS (+ COACH for the Coach user); PROGRAM is gone. `ProgramsPage.tsx` (replaces `ProgramPage.tsx`; `/program`, from an icon in Plan's header and the planner's back links): saved programs (create; OPEN IN PLANNER → `/program/:id`; per-row START → the name sheet → `useStartRun`/`v2_start_run`, which ends an active run atomically), the active run (END RUN), completed runs (delete; row → `/meso/:id/priorities`). `handleStartMeso` now has try/catch.
- Sequence runs (chunk 25): `v2_program_sequence_items` (workout and rest slots; a workout may repeat); one week plan per slot by `(workout_day_id, sequence_position)` (037; weekday rows keep it null); cycles are week plans (`week_number` = cycle). `sequenceSchedule.ts` (pure) decides the next slot; Today is `SequenceTodayPage` (TRAIN ANYWAY, SKIP); Plan's current cycle is the next due slot's (chunk 35, `sequenceLastEvent.ts`). **Every slot-position wiring has a test where the wrong slot changes the result.** Full line: HISTORY.md, "2026-10-14 staging setup".
- Optional Start Set flow (`measure_set_time`): `setTimerStore`, freezes true rest, captures `set_seconds`; floating `RestTimer` plus `RestTimerInline` under the just-logged row.
- Rest chain (chunk 16): `restChain.ts` `resolveRestTarget` (pure) picks the timer target: set override → on the exercise's last planned set its "rest after" → exercise rest → global; supersets: no timer inside a round unless the set or block says so, round-end = block override or the ending exercise's chain, "rest after" only after the block's final round; staged: only while a next stage is to come, kind default (dropset none, others 15 s) or `stage_rest_seconds`. A null `stage_kind` is **not** promoted to dropset for rest (D30: legacy dropsets keep the global timer; pinned by a real-session test). `restTimerStore.startRest(seconds)` sets `targetSeconds` (read by `RestTimer`); `start()` is unchanged (Settings target); "no timer" calls `stop()`. GymSession batches the run copy's `v2_program_sets` (`useProgramSets`) and block rests (`useSupersetBlockRests`) once per screen; edited in the shared `StepExercises`/`StepVolume`.
- Tempo (chunk 17): `v2_program_exercises.tempo`, edited by `TempoEditor` beside REST/REST AFTER in `StepExercises` (validated only by `normaliseTempo`; invalid → inline error, nothing written; blank → null; never gated by `volumeReadOnly`); `ExerciseHeader` shows it beside the name, rendering nothing when null (D30). Never on a log row. Carried by the G14 clone.
- Warmup routine (chunk 18): `warmupRoutineService.ts` is the only reader/writer of `v2_workout_warmup_items` (two-phase offset reorder under the unique position index; remove re-packs). Edited below the exercise list in `StepExercises` (never gated by `volumeReadOnly`). `WarmupRoutineChecklist` at the top of `GymSession` renders nothing with no items (D30). Ticks: `warmupRoutineStore` (Zustand) mirrored to localStorage key `overload:warmup-routine-ticks:<sessionId>`, try/catch everywhere, 20 most recent sessions kept; never sent to Supabase, Dexie or the queue. `v2_copy_program` copies items to run copies; the G14 clone copies them too.
- Week targets and tags (chunk 19): weight target (exercise's unit in, kg stored; heads and stages), the week's rep-target override (`parseRepTarget`; writes only the week-plan set) and tags on heads (`PRESET_TAGS` + custom; `addTag`/`removeTag`/`applyTagToAllHeads` in `plannerVocabulary.ts` — dedupe exact, last removed → null; apply-to-all skips warmups and stages). AMRAP with a null RIR gets RIR 0 in the same update (`applyAmrapRirDefault`), never overwriting one. The workout screen's `SetRow` shows `TARGET WEIGHT` (exercise's unit) and tags only on sets that have them (nothing rendered otherwise; tags are display-only, never logged); `PlanTargetsPanel` shows weight beside RIR. Tags are never copied (`copySetsWithGrouping`, `v2_plan_week`). The shared `useUpdateSet` is `networkMode: 'always'`.
- Apply ahead (chunk 20; 1.2 removes it in chunk 53): `applyAhead.ts` (pure) turns one `ChangeRecord` + later planned weeks into ops or a skip; a later row matches by its own id **and** current `exerciseId`; `useApplyAhead` runs ops through `weekPlanService`, stopping at the first failure; offer in `ApplyAheadOffer.tsx`; `apply()` is single-flight (B6). **Every new edit type must extend `applyAhead.ts`, its tests and a screen-layer record test.** Full line: HISTORY.md, "2026-10-14 staging verified".
- Deload per session (chunk 21): `v2_week_plans.is_deload` is the session's flag. Plan keeps the per-session toggle and adds MARK WEEK AS DELOAD / UNMARK THIS WEEK (`useSetWeekDeload`: `planWeek` first, then `setWeekDeload` on every row of `(meso, week)`); a shared (G14) row shows "Marks Mon, … — they share one plan". Today, preview and workout screen say "DELOAD" per session (Progress' chart legend still says DELOAD WEEK for a week region, by design). Copy sources and apply-ahead skip deload sessions.
- Deload rules (chunk 22; 1.2 moves them to Settings only, chunk 48): `src/lib/deloadRules.ts` (pure) validates, resolves precedence (run program's `deload_rules` → user's → none), calculates sets/weight/reps/RIR and finds the base occurrence; mark with rules snapshots to `deload_restore` first, unmark restores then clears (B5); a started session is flag-only. Full line: HISTORY.md, "2026-10-14 staging verified".
- Finish: `useAutoFinishSession` (30 s poll, grace window after reopen) and manual finish both use `deriveCompletedAt` (max `logged_at`; null with no eligible logs); `SessionComplete` captures energy/pump; note editable after completion; an all-skipped session completes as `skipped`.
- Finished-session screen (`CompletedTodayScreen`): CONTINUE SESSION (reopen, after a confirm) and the note editor only; it takes `session`, `workoutDay`, `weekNumber`, `todayLabel`, `onBack`, `scheduleType`. **REDO SESSION was removed 2026-10-10 (B1, DECISIONS 78):** its CONFIRM marked the finished session `skipped` with its sets kept and started a fresh one. Nothing on this screen skips or creates a session (tests pin it). A `skipped` row of today's own workout still doesn't block a fresh START suggestion (`scheduler.ts`, unchanged).
- Swap exercise (session-only): `SwapExerciseSheet` + `exerciseSwapLogic.ts`; writes `v2_session_exercise_swaps`, skips the original's remaining sets, shows one merged card with prefill from the original's plan.
- Add exercise mid-workout: same sheet in `'add'` mode (muscle-group filter chips, excludes exercises already active); card lives in local state until its first set is logged, then is rebuilt from logs (`extraExercises`).
- `WorkoutSidebarSheet` (Coach user only): NOTES tab (raw Coach Notes, optionally session-scoped) and ASK tab (in-session Q&A via `QaPanel`).

**Plan / Program**
- `PlanPage`: `WorkoutSwitcher` chip row (one workout day at a time), per-set RIR targets and dropset stages, deload flag (one `v2_week_plans.is_deload` per workout per week, toggled per workout panel once that workout has a plan row; copying carries the flag into the new week), whole-week COPY WEEK and single-workout copy (shared `copyOnePlanForward` → `copySetsWithGrouping`; COPY offered only when the destination is empty and the source has rows). No COMPACT view (removed in chunk 29).
- **Plan week panel (chunks 29–30; standing UI rule; 1.2 rebuilds it in chunk 54):** page-level actions above each workout panel, then SETS / STRUCTURE (`SegmentBar`, opens on SETS, page-local); SETS: number, weight, reps, RIR, ⋯ → tags + DELETE SET; STRUCTURE: exercise ⋯ (swap, move, warmups, remove, run-wide REST / REST AFTER / TEMPO, UNIT), set ⋯ (stages, warmup delete, REST where G45 (c) allows), links, the warmup routine. Run-wide writes go to each exercise's own row (`designFieldEditors.tsx`, `StructureFields.tsx`). Past weeks read-only. Tests: `planMenus.testutil.ts`. Full line: HISTORY.md, "2026-10-14 staging verified".
- Programs and runs: saved programs are edited in the stepped planner (`/program/:id`, chunks 10–11); starting one is `v2_start_run` (chunk 6: copies it to a run, ends any active run atomically); a run's copy is edited only through the week (Structure view; Make default); the planner refuses it (chunk 33). - `src/lib/plannerVocabulary.ts` (chunk 2): the planner's fixed vocabularies — set kinds (`deriveSetKind` from a head's `isWarmup`/`stageKind`; `resolveStageKind` reads a null kind as dropset), `STAGE_KINDS` (`dropset|rest_pause|myo_reps|cluster`) with `DEFAULT_STAGE_REST_SECONDS` (dropset null, others 15) and `STAGE_KIND_CARRIES_WEIGHT`, `PRESET_TAGS` (SPEC order), rep target (`parseRepTarget`/`formatRepTarget`, `repTargetToColumns`/`columnsToRepTarget`; `formatRepTarget` of none returns the text `none` — SPEC: a set without a target shows no target, so UI must not print it), `normaliseTempo` (four fields, digits or `X`, lowercase `x` accepted and normalised, ≤ 20 chars; `parseRepTarget` folds any casing of `amrap`/`none` — DECISIONS 34), `DEFAULT_DELOAD_SETS_RULE`, `DEFAULT_DELOAD_WEIGHT_RULE` (`{ percent: 75, rounding: 'down', step: 2.5, stepUnit: 'kg' }` — DECISIONS 33). The workout screen (`GymSession`, `SetGroup`, `SetRow`), `restChain.ts` and the planner read these values from here; literals are not duplicated.

**Tooling and tests**

### From CONTEXT.md: Repo facts → ignoreCommand bullet (shortened)
- `vercel.json` `ignoreCommand` (166 characters; limit 256; D28, B4 #81): `test -n "$VERCEL_GIT_PREVIOUS_SHA" && git cat-file -e "$VERCEL_GIT_PREVIOUS_SHA" 2>/dev/null && git diff --quiet "$VERCEL_GIT_PREVIOUS_SHA" HEAD -- . ':(exclude)*.md'`. It skips the build only when nothing but `.md` files changed since the last deployed commit; an empty variable or a SHA outside the shallow clone builds. `scripts/vercel-ignore.test.mjs` runs it in throwaway repos (staging and renamed `.md` docs included: it reads no branch name, and `VERCEL_GIT_PREVIOUS_SHA` is the same branch's last deploy, empty on a branch's first deploy, which builds). Seen on a real push 2026-10-14: #87's docs-only merge to master read "Canceled by Ignored Build Step". A changed design PNG is not `.md` and builds.

### From CONTEXT.md: Staging and the 1.2 build → Release (shortened; the full checklist is in TASKS-1.2.md)
**Release** (all of it Adam's go-ahead)

Tag `v1.2.0`, GitHub Release with the notes.

Builders work in that checkout. Do reviewer checks in a `git worktree` under the scratchpad. ### From CONTEXT.md: Checks that lied → #5 and #8 in full (the lessons stay in CONTEXT.md)
5. **Browser `left_click` reporting success or timing out** without firing a click event (found 2026-08-25; also in mobile-viewport emulation). Verify resulting state; a programmatic `element.click()` via `javascript_tool` is a disclosed exception, not a substitute. Coordinate clicks landed on wrong elements. Computer-screenshot compositing can return stale frames.
8. **A successful push.** `ignoreCommand` compared `HEAD` to `HEAD^` and silently skipped a deploy whose last commit was docs-only (2026-08-31); it was replaced by a `$VERCEL_GIT_PREVIOUS_SHA` version, then on 2026-09-29 (because that version exceeded Vercel's 256-character limit) by the `HEAD^` form again; #81 (2026-10-11) restored the previous-SHA comparison in 166 characters. Confirm a deploy landed at four levels: `vercel ls` (a real build, not a 2 s "Canceled" row), `vercel inspect` on the canonical alias (`Ready`, production), the function list, and a grep of the deployed bundle for new strings (and absence of old ones).

### From CONTEXT.md: Rules → the break-proof and sheet-overflow rules before chunk 40's review added to them
- **Break proofs restore from a `cp` backup, never `git checkout --`** on a file with uncommitted changes. Checkout reverts every uncommitted edit, not just the break; chunk 9's builder silently lost its fix that way and caught it by md5. A break is one exact replacement that must match once: one that never fired reads as caught (chunk 39).
- **The 375 px `scrollWidth` check is blind inside a sheet** (chunk 39; reproduced): a `position: fixed` layer never changes `document.scrollWidth`, so a 700 px block in a `BottomSheet` reads `scrollWidth 375: ok`. For a sheet, prove 375 px inside the dialog in Chromium on the chunk's fixtures: no descendant past the dialog's edges, no element wider inside than it shows, and a control (a 700 px block in the dialog) that fails. `screenshot-fixture.mjs` doesn't measure it yet (a builder's change, in no chunk's scope). A long-text probe needs a word with no break opportunity: a hyphenated 80-character name wrapped and passed where 80 of one letter overflowed.

21. **Hand-typed fixture dates** (2026-10-03): a scheduler scenario dated its "Friday" session 2026-09-26 (a Saturday) and left a Wednesday unhandled, so three scenarios returned `missed_sessions` the scheduler hadn't caused. Derive fixture dates from the weekday and print the queue, not just the result type.
22. **An injected failure that never fired** (2026-10-03): a CHECK added to force a mid-copy failure couldn't be created (existing rows violated it), so the "atomicity" run simply succeeded. Confirm the injected error's text appears before reading "nothing persisted" as proof; a `NOT VALID` constraint injects on new rows only.
24. **Waiting on one check-run id** (2026-10-04): the `Supabase Preview` run first seen on 027's merge commit stayed `in_progress` indefinitely while a later run on the same commit had already succeeded; a watcher keyed to the first id would have waited forever. Read all runs of a check by name on the commit, and confirm a deploy by its effect (`probe-live-columns.mjs`).
25. **Replay green, scratch checks green, every new column live — and the app broke** (2026-10-04): 027's second `v2_mesocycles → v2_programs` FK made `fetchMesos`'s embed ambiguous (`PGRST201`), so production showed no mesocycles. SQL-level checks can't see PostgREST relationship resolution; `check-embeds-local.sh` can (DECISIONS 38).
26. **A live check scoped to Adam's user_id, read as "no such data exists"** (2026-10-05): L6 found no program with one workout on two weekdays, so G14 was declared void — but Adam has a second account, which has exactly that. Every Adam-scoped live result describes his main account only; say so when using it to rule a case out, and don't call a spec gap void on it.
27. **A green required check on a PR that still read `blocked`** (2026-10-05): after #23 was retargeted to master, `migration-replay` was started by `workflow_dispatch` on its head and passed, but GitHub kept the PR `blocked`. The dispatched run didn't count as the PR's check. And the stacked branch turned out to lack two master merges (#20, #21), so the dispatched run had tested a tree master would never get. A PR's checks count only when the PR's own `pull_request` run passes on the merged tree.
28. **"Compared by hand"** (2026-10-06): chunk 9's builder reported TS and SQL copies "structurally identical" after reading both. An executed comparison on 6 scenarios was needed before it counted. The double-swap carry bug was in exactly the part a reading glosses over (the existing carry). Parity claims need an executed comparison.
30. **A D30-safety rule proven only in a pure module** (2026-10-07): chunk 16 kept legacy null-kind dropsets on the global timer, with a resolver unit test, but the hook that maps `stage_kind` into the resolver was untested — promoting null to dropset there passed all 1110 tests. A compatibility rule needs a real-session test at the layer that applies it, not just at the pure function.
31. **An unbounded history query under PostgREST's row cap** (2026-10-08): chunk 23's cross-run reference query read every set log for the screen's exercises with no order and no paging; `max_rows = 1000` (supabase/config.toml) would silently return an arbitrary 1000 once history grew, dropping last week's session. Every history read either pages (ordered, `.range()` until a short page) or is bounded.
32. **A passing test that asserted the bug** (2026-10-10, B2): `MoveSessionSheet.test.tsx` had "offers all 7 days of the session's own week", written to the chunk's wording, so a sheet offering past days passed green for a whole chunk. When a rule is "only X", test what must be *absent*, on a day where something is already past (today's own weekday decides what's past).

### From DECISIONS.md: entry 131 in full, as it stood before Adam's answer (answered 2026-10-15: (b))
### 131 G56: after a week off, Plan can't reach the current week (weekday runs)
**Ask:** what should Plan show when a past week was never planned? On a weekday run a week is planned only when the app plans it: Plan opening on it (chunk 52 plans only the current week) or a workout starting. A calendar week in which neither happens (a week off) is never planned. SPEC says the tiles run "from week 1 to the first unplanned one", "Nothing beyond the first unplanned week is reachable", and Plan "opens on the current week": after a week off the current week lies beyond the unplanned one, so these can't all hold. Built in chunk 42 (`weekTiles`): the tiles stop at the unplanned past week, so the current week has no tile until every missed week is planned forward.
**Recommendation:** (b): it keeps "opens on the current week", writes nothing for a week nobody trained, and the source rules already pass over a week with no plan, so the current week is planned from the last week that has one.
**Blocks:** chunk 42's merge (`build/chunk-42` at `1065cbb`; the rest of the chunk passed review) and chunk 52 (the tiles, planning on open, PLAN FORWARD); with them 43, 53, 54a, 54b, 55, 56, 65, 66, 68 and 69, which need 42 or 52. 44–51b, 57–64 and 67 go on.
**Options:**
- (a) When Plan opens it plans every week that has started and has no plan, oldest first, so no gap stays; `weekTiles` stays as built. The missed week gets the structure and no numbers (044), becomes the next week's source and COPY's "last week", and COPY then finds no numbers to copy.
- (b) The tiles run from week 1 through the current week whatever is planned, then the weeks planned ahead and the first unplanned one after the current week; a missed week's tile reads NOT PLANNED and opens read-only, empty, with no PLAN FORWARD; nothing is ever written for it. `weekTiles` changes (one rule and its tests: a builder retry, then review); how that tile looks is a display choice for 52.
- (c) As built: the tiles stop at the first unplanned week even when it is past; the current week (planned when Plan opens) can't be reached until each missed week is planned forward, one at a time, which writes past weeks with (a)'s COPY problem.
**Answer:**
**Evidence:** SPEC, Weeks and copying: "When a week (cycle) gets planned (2): when it starts, or earlier when the user taps PLAN FORWARD on it. Opening it doesn't plan it."; "How far ahead: Plan shows every week from week 1 to the last planned week, plus one more: the first week not planned yet … Nothing beyond the first unplanned week is reachable." Screens → Plan: "a tile per week (cycle) from week 1 to the first unplanned one, scrolling sideways; it opens on the current week." TASKS-1.2 chunk 42 pins planned {1,2,4} → tiles 1, 2, 3 without naming the current week (its Goal's "from 1 to `max(planned) + 1`" would give 1–5); chunk 52 plans "only the current week … when it has no rows", and Today's START and the missed-session prompt plan only the current week (F1). Nothing plans a week that starts while the app is closed, and a weekday run's week number is the calendar week since its start, so one week without Plan or a workout leaves a gap. A sequence run can't have one: a cycle only becomes past once each of its workouts is started or skipped, and starting or skipping one plans its cycle. The builder built (c), pinned it ("a current week beyond the tiles has no THIS tile": planned {1,2}, current week 6 → tiles 1, 2, 3) and raised it as a possible gap. It decides what Plan lets you reach and, under (a) and (c), what is written for past weeks, so D31 doesn't cover it. Cost: (a) and (c) change nothing in 42 (52 builds them); (b) changes `weekTiles` before 42 merges.

### From CONTEXT.md: Staging and the 1.2 build → lines replaced by shorter ones, and "Staging verification" (setup, finished)
- Staging matches production in Postgres version, pg-safeupdate behaviour and migration history (checked at setup, not assumed). It holds no real person's data — never Adam's friend's, never Northstar's, not Adam's own (the repo is public and the seed is committed). Sign-ups are off; only accounts the setup creates sign in. The test account's password never enters the repo. It looks different (badge, PWA name and icon). It proves mechanics and screens; a week of real use still follows the release.
- `supabase/seed.sql`: synthetic data for the staging accounts, covering every data shape SPEC and TASKS-1.2 name (its header lists them; TASKS-1.2 "Seed": what each chunk relies on and what the seed still lacks). Dates are relative to the day it runs: since Adam's re-seed (2026-10-14) the test account's week 3 (stable's week 2, sequence's cycle 2) is the week of Monday 2026-10-12, past from Monday 2026-10-19. **A changed seed reaches staging only when Adam pastes it into the staging branch's SQL editor** (it rebuilds the accounts' data and keeps the accounts; `[remotes.staging]` has `db.seed` on).
- `scripts/staging-smoke.mjs` (env `STAGING_SUPABASE_URL`, `STAGING_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `STAGING_TEST_PASSWORD`): sign-ups off, the four sign-in accounts sign in, the seed's shapes (55 checks since chunk 36, the stable, sequence and empty accounts and week 2's differences included), no account sees another's rows, pg-safeupdate; break-proven on a local stack. A seed change updates its expectations in the same chunk. On staging: 54/55 since chunk 37's review, the one failure "empty: owns no exercises — 46" (DECISIONS 125), not a regression.
- **On staging since Adam's re-seed (2026-10-14, DECISIONS 124):** `staging-stable@example.com` (`…0003`: STG Full Body, an active stable run; week 1 done, Full Body Tue and Thu on one shared plan row (G14), Arms Sat; week 2 planned, nothing done; global deload rules on), `staging-sequence@example.com` (`…0004`: STG Rotation, an active sequence run; cycle 1 done, cycle 2 planned, Rotation A due on the seed's day), `staging-empty@example.com` (`…0005`: only the app's 46 default exercises, DECISIONS 125). `STAGING_TEST_PASSWORD` signs in to all four. Long form: HISTORY.md, "2026-10-15 chunk 44 review".
- Per-chunk mode (2026-10-14): a subagent cannot start a subagent here (probed: the Agent tool is absent inside a subagent), so the coordinator starts each chunk's builder itself, then a fresh reviewer subagent (opus, max effort) with the chunk number and the builder's report; the reviewer reviews, merges, runs the staging steps and updates CONTEXT.md / DECISIONS.md.
- After each schema merge the reviewer checks the Supabase deploy on the staging branch succeeded (Dashboard → Branches log is Adam's; on GitHub, the `Supabase Preview` runs on the merge commit, read every run). **A failed staging deploy is blocking.** Then every table the migration added must answer `200` (not `42501`) to an anon `select … limit=0` on staging; `verify-rls` counts `42501` as a pass, so it can't catch a missing grant.
- Models (Adam, 2026-10-14): coordinator and batch reviewers on Opus 5.5 at max effort; builders on Sonnet 5.5 at `effort: max` through `.claude/agents/builder.md` (on `staging` since #86; `model: claude-sonnet-5-5`; one chunk per run on `build/chunk-<N>` off `staging`, final commit "chunk N complete", a brief report) (DECISIONS 120).
- Works: push to new branches, open and merge PRs (MCP GitHub tools; `gh api` REST, not GraphQL), `git worktree`, Docker (start `dockerd`; Docker Hub pulls work), Playwright + Chromium (the global `playwright@1.56.1` under `/opt/node-tools/node_modules`, Chromium at `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome`, `HTTPS_PROXY` as the launch proxy, the bypass header only on requests to the staging host), `isolation: 'worktree'` (no nested subagents: per-chunk mode). A fresh container has no `node_modules`: `npm ci` first.
**Staging verification** (setup, 2026-10-14; the record is in HISTORY.md): Postgres production 17.6, staging 17.11 (DECISIONS 123); default privileges (#90) cover only objects `postgres` owns, so the per-merge `200`-not-`42501` check proves a new table's grants.

### From CONTEXT.md: Repo facts → Stack, Supabase deploys, ignoreCommand, Vercel env vars and Docs; Open items → the Coach-era and still-open lines, in the form they had
- Stack: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, vite-plugin-pwa; Tailwind CSS v4 + tokens.css (all colours as CSS custom properties); Supabase JS v2 (auth + database); TanStack Query v5 (server state); Zustand v5 (UI state only — rest timer, pending sync IDs); Dexie v4 (offline cache); Recharts v3; date-fns v4; React Router v6; Lucide React. 1.2 adds one devDependency, `playwright-core` 1.56.1 (exact; chunk 37, TASKS-1.2 "Additions to the core stack"), for `npm run shot`; nothing else.
- Supabase deploys migrations from master (the GitHub integration on project `imhsawrghteqsmpklofv`, production branch `master`, Automatic branching off): a push to master applies the files not yet in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`, in order; seed and config never reach production; production's history lists `000`–`041` (DECISIONS 121). The result shows as the **`Supabase Preview`** check on master's merge commit (`skipped` on PR commits; several runs can appear: read every run and confirm by effect, `probe-live-columns.mjs`); anything but success, or no check within a few minutes, is a failed deploy until Adam has read the Dashboard → Branches log.
- `vercel.json` `ignoreCommand` (166 characters; limit 256; D28, B4 #81) skips the build only when nothing but `.md` files changed since the last deployed commit (`$VERCEL_GIT_PREVIOUS_SHA`; an empty variable or a SHA outside the shallow clone builds). `scripts/vercel-ignore.test.mjs` runs it in throwaway repos. A docs-only merge reads "Canceled by Ignored Build Step" (seen on #87); a changed design PNG builds.
- Set Vercel env vars with `vercel env add` (more reliable than dashboard automation) and redeploy for them to take effect.
- Docs: SPEC.md = the Overload Planner Extension spec ([P1], [P1.1], [1.2]; "Superseded by 1.2"; "Design boards [1.2]": boards decide layout, order and wording, SPEC wins, never pixel-match). TASKS-1.2.md = the [1.2] plan; TASKS.md = phase 1; TASKS-1.1.md = [P1.1]; RETRO-phase-1.md; the v3 and v2 SPEC/TASKS pairs (shipped; comments before 2026-10-03 citing "SPEC.md §n" mean v3); AUDIT.md; the Coach-era initiatives each have their own SPEC/TASKS pair; COACH-EXERCISE-TAGS.md is the approved tag list.

### From DECISIONS.md: "Waiting on Adam" as it stood before this review
*Rewritten at every boundary. Last: 2026-10-15, chunk 42 merged (#109, `d602dbc`) after a builder retry of `weekTiles` for your answer to 131 (G56). New: 135, a to-do: lines of SPEC.md and TASKS-1.2.md written before that answer still say otherwise for a past week nobody planned; amend them to defer to 131? Still open: 133, which blocks chunk 44's merge and chunk 55. Items 82–112 are 1.1's provisional display choices (D31), each built as written unless you change it. Each list is ordered by what it blocks.*

Decisions:
- **133** — VOLUME: what a workout of last week counts when the week is over and the workout was never done (never started, moved and never started, or started and never finished) and never marked skipped. SPEC: "Last week's number is what was actually done … sessions not done yet count their plan"; built: it counts its plan, so a missed workout reads as done to plan, with no note. Recommended: (b) once last week is over it counts what was done (nothing, or the sets an unfinished session logged), so the note shows what was missed; while last week is still running, as built. Blocks: chunk 44's merge and chunk 55; nothing else (55 comes after 54b).
- **125** — the empty staging account now owns the app's 46 default exercises (the app creates them when an account with none signs in; the reviewer's sign-in did), so `staging-smoke.mjs` reads 54/55. Recommended: (a) "empty" means what a new account has after signing in; the smoke's empty-account check accepts exactly that default set (a small script change). Blocks: nothing before chunk 65; until then every smoke run shows this one expected failure.
- **127** — the 1.2 sheet frame's look where no token or board value decides it. Provisional: the scrim is black at 60 % (no scrim token; the boards draw 45 % light, 70 % dark; 60 % is the app's nearer existing value, behind the Today and workout sheets; TASKS' "look of ProgramsPage's sheet" would be 88 %, heavier than any board); the sheet is `--surface` as the boards and TASKS say (in the dark theme it stands out from the scrimmed page mainly by its border); z-index 45 (the old inline sheets draw above it). Blocks: nothing; the pickers (chunk 39) use the frame, no screen does before chunk 51a.
- **128** — the three pickers' display choices where SPEC and the boards give no value (chunk 39). Provisional: stage stepper 1–10; rest steppers 15 s a tap up to 10:00, as the app's existing rest stepper; a segment opens on the boards' examples (8, 8–10, RIR 2, 1–2); the number boxes are steppers, not inputs; "Use for all" not drawn under two sets; a kind change keeps the stage count and the rest between stages; text on the accent is `--base` (near-white on orange in the light theme, about 2.2:1; the boards draw near-black); an unbroken word of 35+ characters runs past its line. Blocks: nothing; no screen uses the pickers before 51a / 54a.
- **129** — the cues sheet's choices where SPEC and board 8 give no value (chunk 40). Provisional: "+ NEW CUE" opens an input in its place with an ADD button (no board draws it: `design/1.2/built/8-new-cue.png`); a typed cue that matches a preset or one of your own cues, ignoring case, ticks that row instead of adding a second cue that reads the same; "Use for all" counts working sets only and isn't drawn under two; text on the accent is `--base` (as 128); no length limit on a cue. Not a choice, so you see it: "Use for all" adds the ticked cues to the other working sets and removes none (TASKS' answer), so an untick changes this set only. Blocks: nothing; no screen opens the sheet before 54a / 61.
- **130** — the exercise picker's choices where the boards differ or give no value (chunk 41). Provisional: one look for every caller (W11's hairline rows and muted chips; PL4–PL6 draw cards and solid chips); the group under each name unless the caller turns it off; always the tall sheet; PP2d's list not edge to edge; a tap on the chip that is on goes back to ALL; an exercise created in the sheet counts as a tap on its row; words for states no board draws (LOADING…, COULDN'T LOAD EXERCISES and the reason, NO OTHER EXERCISES, "No exercises yet."); only the field while a new exercise saves; a 16 px name field; text on the accent `--base` (as 128 (g)); W11's line over the button doesn't break a name with no space (as 128 (i)). Blocks: nothing; no screen opens the picker before 51a / 59 / 68.
- **132** — chunk 42's display choices where SPEC gives no rule (chunk 42 merged, #109). Provisional: a box that differs from its source is marked even when it is empty, so a week planned forward reads as changed in every number, with "CHANGED SINCE WEEK N", until COPY or typing fills it; an unplanned current week's tile reads NOT PLANNED and offers no PLAN FORWARD (Plan plans it as it opens); a warmup's RIR is never marked (G49); THIS WEEK ONLY counts a stage's rep target too; "last week" for the marks is the workout's last normal, non-empty week (a missed week passed over). Not choices, so you see them: week 1 of a week-dependent run keeps the program's rep targets; COPY never empties a box, writes only the ticked fields and copies each workout from its last normal week (after a missed week too, as 131 says). ### 133 VOLUME: what a missed workout of a week that is over counts (chunk 44)
**Ask:** when last week is over (Plan on the current week), what does VOLUME count for one of its workouts that was never done and never marked skipped: never started (no session), moved and never started (`planned`), or started and never finished (`in_progress`)? SPEC 14: "Last week's number is what was actually done: done sessions count their done sets (added sets in, skipped ones out); sessions not done yet count their plan." Chunk 44 built TASKS 44's words, "a session not done counts its plan", for every week: such a workout counts its plan, so last week reads as done to plan there, with no note.

Under (a), a week nobody trained reads as done to plan if Plan was opened in it, and as nothing if it wasn't.
**Blocks:** chunk 44's merge (`build/chunk-44` at `073bd21`; everything else in it passed review) and chunk 55 (the VOLUME sheet). Nothing else: 55 comes after 54b, and no other chunk calls the module.
**Options:**
- (a) As built: a workout not completed or skipped counts its plan whether or not last week is over. 44 merges as it is.
- (b) Once last week is over, a workout not done counts what was done: nothing if it was never started, the sets it logged if it was started and never finished; its plan still counts in "YOU PLANNED …", so the note shows what was missed. While last week is still running (Plan on a week planned ahead), not-done workouts count their plan, as built. `volumeRows` takes whether last week is over (55 passes it: it is over exactly when Plan shows the current week); a builder retry of that branch and its tests.
**Answer:**

The module takes no date, so it can't tell a workout still to come from one missed. Pinned as built by the tests "no session created for its plan yet", "in progress", "planned (moved, not started)", "mixed: Monday done, Wednesday in progress, Friday not started" and the G14 "Thursday not created yet" / "Thursday in progress"; the reviewer's break that counts nothing for a workout with no session fails six of them.
