### From DECISIONS.md: 142, in full, with Adam's answer
### 142 A CHANGE THE PROGRAM save on a session marked deload (chunk 45)
**Ask:** A session marked deload with deload rules on keeps a saved copy of its plan from before the marking, and UNMARK puts that copy back whole: it deletes the session's sets and re-inserts the copy. CHANGE THE PROGRAM changes every session that hasn't started, a deload one included (SPEC), but nothing changes that saved copy. So after a save that removes, swaps or adds an exercise, unmarking the deload brings back the sets of the removed or swapped-out exercise (sets the session's exercise list no longer names, so Plan doesn't show them) and leaves the swapped-in or added exercise with no sets. What should a save do to a not-started session that is marked deload?
**Recommendation:** (a): the save changes the saved copy the same way it changes the session, so UNMARK restores the plan as it stands after the change. It keeps both of SPEC's sentences true ("It applies to every session that isn't done yet"; unmarking "restores what was planned before it was marked"). It costs one more table on 043's list (chunk 47, not built yet: `v2_week_plans`, update of `deload_restore` only) and, in chunk 45, the same rules run over each deload session's saved copy.
**Blocks:** chunk 45's merge (every option changes what it writes) and so the chunks that need 45: 47 (its op type; under (a) and (c) 043's table list grows), 50, 51a, 51b and 56, and after them 52, 65, 66, 53, 54a, 54b, 55, 68, 69. 50 needs only `runSchedule.ts`, which no answer changes: merging that file on its own would be a scope change, yours to allow. Not blocked: 46, 48, 49, 57, 58a–64, 67.
**Options:**
- (a) As recommended: the saved copy changes with the session.
- (b) A not-started session marked deload is left exactly as it is, like one in progress, and the rule box names it. It keeps the old exercises (a removed or swapped-out one included) until it is unmarked; 45 takes each session's deload flag.
- (c) The change lands on the session and its saved copy is dropped: UNMARK then only clears the flag and keeps the deload's reduced sets (043 may set `deload_restore` to null).
- (d) As built: the change lands on the session and the saved copy stays as it was (the probe below). Not recommended: unmarking writes sets of exercises the session no longer has.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-15) "(a), narrowed. A CHANGE THE PROGRAM save also applies its landing rules to the saved pre-deload copy of a not-started deload session, so UNMARK restores the plan with the change in it. Migration 043's executor may write v2_week_plans for that one column only, as an update only: no insert or delete on v2_week_plans, no other column. A patch touching any other v2_week_plans column is rejected like a protected column, with a test."
**Evidence:** SPEC, Programs and runs: "It applies to every session that isn't done yet, from the current week (cycle) on, including a week already planned forward … Done sessions keep their plan."; How a save lands: "'Not done' means not started: a session in progress is left exactly as it is."; Deload: "Unmarking a session whose sets the rules calculated restores what was planned before it was marked." Neither SPEC nor TASKS-1.2 says what a save does to a deload session or its saved copy, and TASKS 47's table list has no `v2_week_plans`, so no op can change the copy. The app: `markSessionDeload` saves the session's sets to `v2_week_plans.deload_restore` before replacing them; `unmarkSessionDeload` → `applyDeloadRestore` deletes every set of the session and inserts the saved ones by their `program_exercise_id` (`weekPlanService.ts`). A session marked with rules off has no saved copy and isn't affected. The reviewer's executed probe (the builder's in-memory executor with the app's own `applyDeloadRestore` and `insertRestoredPlanSets`): the stable test world, week 3's Full Body marked deload (sets −50 %), then one save removing Incline Dumbbell Press, swapping Leg Press and adding an exercise. The deload session took the change; after UNMARK it held 5 sets of the two exercises it no longer lists, and the swapped-in and added exercises had none. The week-dependent world (week 3's Pull, one removal and one swap): 6 such sets. 1.1's week-level remove and swap had the same path (neither touched the saved copy); sets written outside a session's own exercise list were fixed once before as a data bug (deload marking, chunk 22; HISTORY.md). Under (a), (c) and (d) a stable exercise added in a deload session gets the default's full sets, not a deload calculation. The builder raised it (its report, 3.A.1).

### From DECISIONS.md: 143, in full, with Adam's answer
### 143 After a change, what a week-dependent workout's next week is copied from (chunk 45)
**Ask:** In a week-dependent program, a new week of a workout is copied from that workout's last planned normal week, whether its session is done or not. If you change the program after that session is done or started (say Monday's Push is done, and on Tuesday you remove Face Pull from Push), the save can change nothing that next week's Push will be copied from: the done session keeps its plan. So next week's Push gets Face Pull back, misses an exercise you added and undoes a swap. SPEC says the change applies "to what later weeks are copied from". How should such a change reach the workout's later weeks?
**Recommendation:** (a): a week-dependent week is copied from its last planned normal week with the program's current exercise list laid over it: an exercise the program removed is left out, one it added comes with no sets, and the program's order is used. A change then always reaches later weeks, as SPEC says, the way it already does on stable programs (their weeks copy from the program). A swap needs the copy to know what the new exercise replaced, which the program doesn't record today: either a stored link (a new column, so a migration) or, cheaper, (a′).
**Blocks:** chunk 45's merge (under (a) it records the swap; under (b) its ops and under (c) its texts change) and so the chunks that need 45, as in 142; also, under (a) or (a′), chunk 53 (044's copy rule) and chunk 42's merged `autoCopy`.
**Options:**
- (a) As recommended, with the swap link (a migration).
- (a′) The same, with a swap reached this way arriving as a new exercise with no sets.
- (b) When a workout has no not-started session left from the current week on, the save plans its next week at once, as PLAN FORWARD would, and lands the change there. A save then plans a week, which SPEC's "When a week (cycle) gets planned" doesn't list, and 043 would have to insert week plans.
- (c) As built: a change reaches only sessions already planned and not started; next week copies the done session as it was; the rule box says which workouts the change doesn't reach yet, and SPEC's sentence is reworded.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-15) "(a). A week-dependent week copied after a save follows the run copy's current exercise list and order: an exercise still in the program brings its sets from the source session as the copy rules say; a removed one is dropped; an added one arrives with no sets; a swapped one brings the old exercise's sets (count, kinds, stages, rep targets — as SPEC's swap rule). The link is the run copy's program exercise row: if the week's exercises already point at it and a swap updates that row in place, use that; add a stored link only if a swap deletes and re-inserts the row, and say which it was in the chunk report. Copying also goes in programChange/weekPlanning tests and in 044's rules, each with a break-proven test."
**Evidence:** SPEC, Programs and runs: "It applies to every session that isn't done yet, from the current week (cycle) on, including a week already planned forward, and to what later weeks are copied from. Done sessions keep their plan."; Weeks and copying: "Source, `week-dependent`: the last planned normal occurrence"; "Week-dependent weeks (1a): … A change carries forward through the next auto-copy"; 131's answer: "The current week copies from the last planned normal week, as the copy rules already say" (it keeps the source rule and doesn't speak to a save). TASKS 45 lands a save "on the run copy and on every not-done session from the current week on"; TASKS 42 and 53 keep the week-dependent source ("`weekSources.ts`'s search, kept"); neither says how a save reaches a source that is done. 041's week branch copies the source week's own exercise rows, and its source search has no status filter; chunk 42's `autoCopy` (044's twin) does the same. The reviewer's executed probe: the week-dependent test world with week 3 not yet planned and Pull's week 2 session done (and again in progress); one save removing Face Pull, swapping Lat Pulldown and adding an exercise changed no session (Pull had none not started; the rule box's week was 2, from Push and Legs). `autoCopy` for week 3's Pull then gave Lat Pulldown ×3 and Face Pull ×2, both removed from the program, and neither new exercise. 51a's card would say "New. It lands in week 2 with no sets" for an exercise that lands in no Pull session. Stable programs are not affected. The builder raised it (its report, 3.A.2).

### 146 Set numbers after a logged set is switched to or from Warmup (chunk 46)
**Ask:** During a workout a logged set's type can be changed (its pen, then SET TYPE; boards W2b, W7a). Warmups are numbered apart from working sets, and a logged set keeps the number it was logged with. When a logged working set becomes a warmup, or a logged warmup becomes a working set, what happens to the working sets' numbers? As built nothing is renumbered, and two rows can show the same number.

### The long form of CONTEXT.md's "CHANGE THE PROGRAM's rules" line (What exists)
- Files: `src/features/programs/programChange.ts` (the op list) and `runSchedule.ts` (the weekday schedule in force per week), with their tests in the same folder: `programChange.{exercises,defaults,runWide,status,weekdays,executed,deload,weekPlansOp,copyAfterSave}.test.ts` and `runSchedule.test.ts`. The worlds and the in-memory stand-in for 043 live in `programChange.testutil.ts` and `programChange.worlds.testutil.ts`; `programChange.deload.testutil.ts` marks and unmarks deload through the app's own `applyCalculatedDeloadMark` / `applyDeloadRestore`, and a test importing it mocks `lib/supabase`. Also `src/features/plan/weekPlanning.ts`'s `autoCopy` week branch (`copyFromWeek`) and `weekPlanning.autoCopy.followsRunCopy.test.ts`. Nothing in the app imports any of it: 47 (`applyOps.ts`), 50 (`useRunSchedule.ts`), 51a / 51b (the screen) and 53 (044, whose twin is `autoCopy`) are the first.
- `planProgramChange({ userId, now, newId, planningType, scheduleType, currentWeek, runCopy, scheduleRows, sessions, edit })` → `{ ops, summary }`. Ops come in this order: inserts of blocks, exercises and program sets, then the run copy's updates, then the routine (parked and placed), then each session's inserts, updates and deletes, then the schedule rows.
- A session is a `v2_week_plans` row with a status from `planRowStatus` (done as soon as any of its sessions is). Done and in-progress sessions are never in an op. An insert row names every NOT NULL column (`created_at` on four tables: RULES.md).
- Each rule is a named branch:
  - added: a run-copy row and, stable, its default's sets in each not-started session;
  - removed: `removed_at`, and the session's sets and exercise row deleted;
  - swapped: a new row at the old place and `removed_at` on the old; the session's rows re-pointed with weight, RIR (both ends) and cues cleared, and on a stable run re-linked to the new row's program sets;
  - reordered: positions, a superset as one block;
  - stable default sets: per set, by link then position, only where the session still equals the old default;
  - run-wide fields: the run copy only;
  - weekdays: `v2_run_schedules` rows and the run copy's `schedule`.
- 142: each not-started session's `deloadRestore` (`WeekPlan.deloadRestore` fits as it is) goes through `landSession` itself. Its entries become planned sets, the set ops are folded back, and one `update v2_week_plans { deload_restore }` is written when the copy changed. `targetRirMax` is kept where an entry has it; a swap clears it to null.
- The op type allows `v2_week_plans` only that update. The stand-in refuses an insert ("insert not allowed"), a delete ("delete not allowed") and any other column ("patch sets a protected column").
- 143: a week-dependent week copied from a week takes the run copy's live rows in their order and positions, and the source week's sets with no numbers:
  - kept: its own sets;
  - removed: left out;
  - added: no sets;
  - swapped: the replaced row's sets, through `replacesProgramExerciseId`, a swap of a swap followed, a loop ending the walk;
  - a source row the run copy doesn't list as live (a 1.1 week-only row) stays after them (DECISIONS 149).
  Until 043's column exists nothing passes the link, so a swapped-in exercise is copied like an added one.
- Review 2: every script green on staging `5ff951d` + the chunk. Breaks: 36 of 36 caught, the control not caught (`<scratchpad>/build/r45b/breaks/`). An executed probe covered 142's UNMARK, the deferral of the link and 149's 1.1 weeks. The follow-up patch for 47 applied and passed (523 tests, `tsc` clean).

### From DECISIONS.md: 150, in full, with Adam's answer
### 150 A set whose type was changed during a workout and then skipped or never logged: a REVIEW item? (chunk 43)
**Ask:** During a workout you change a set's type (SET TYPE in its ⋯: a plain set made a dropset, a dropset with no kind made Normal, a set made a warmup), and then you skip that set or finish without logging it. Next week, should REVIEW also list the type change ("You made set 03 a dropset", USE or IGNORE) beside "Skipped" / "Not logged"? As built (chunk 43's third attempt, `a62a20b`) it doesn't. The set is "Skipped" / "Not logged" only, and when the plan gave it neither a weight nor reps (SPEC lists "Skipped" only where it had them), REVIEW shows nothing about it at all.
**Recommendation:** (b): list it too, read from the set's change row. A set deleted afterwards stays "Skipped" only (your rule: a later delete turns its row into 'deleted'). SPEC 19 says next week sees a type change "only through REVIEW", and 13d's structural items are "for everyone, including people who plan no numbers". Your 141 line says type changes "are seen through the session's change rows". The workout's set type picker (chunk 39, board W7a) already tells you, under the types: "the change shows up in REVIEW when you plan it". Under (a), a plan with no numbers loses the change entirely.
**Blocks:** chunk 43's merge, and so 56, REVIEW's screen. Nothing else: nothing imports `review.ts` before 56, and what chunks 61–63 write is the same under both answers.
**Options:**
- (a) As built: a type change on a set that was then skipped or never logged is not an item. The set is "Skipped" / "Not logged" where the plan had a weight or reps, and nothing where it had neither. Chunk 43 merges as it is, and SPEC's 141 line gets "of a set that was done".
- (b) As recommended: it is also an item, from the set's `retyped` row (its kind, and the count set in the workout). Its USE gives this week's matching set that type, and "Skipped" keeps its own REMOVE THIS SET. This means a fourth builder attempt: a few lines of `sessionItems`, and the one test that pins (a) flips.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-15) "(b). A type change made during a workout is listed in REVIEW even when that set was then skipped or never logged, alongside its "Skipped" / "Not logged" item, and for everyone (13d) — also when the plan gave the set no weight or reps. Chunk 43's fourth attempt builds it; allowed."
**Evidence:** SPEC 13c lists "Skipped" / "Not logged" (only where the plan had a weight or reps); 13d makes "a set type changed (19)" an item, "for everyone"; the 141 line: "a set given a stage kind whose drops or stages weren't done, and a dropset with no kind switched to Normal, are items too. Both are seen through the session's change rows". None of them says whether a set that wasn't done keeps its type item, and 141 was asked about logged sets. The builder read it as needing a set done (its report, 3.4), pinned by the test "a retyped set that was skipped or never logged is 'Skipped' / 'Not logged' alone"; its break D14 (the item from the row) fails exactly two assertions. The reviewer's probe on `a62a20b`: a planned 60 kg × 10–12 set with a `retyped` dropset × 2 row gives "Skipped" or "Not logged" and no type item; planned with no numbers it gives nothing, and so does a kindless dropset switched to Normal and never logged; logged, each is a type item. The builder's other four readings are decided by SPEC or TASKS and stand: a count set in the workout, same kind, extra drops not done, is no item (TASKS 43 judges "a drop/stage added" by "stage logs vs planned stages", and the set type is the kind; if you read a count as a type change, say so with this answer: it is one condition); the change row wins over a log that disagrees (141; in consistent data they agree); an added set given a stage kind is added as that kind ("the done set's kind"); `pending_stages` is a count (TASKS 62). Display: the type item's detail line ("1 drop", "3 pauses"; 139 (b)) now names the count USE writes, also when no drop was done; no string is new. Cost: (a) none; (b) one more builder attempt, about a dozen lines and their tests.

### From DECISIONS.md: 128, in full, with Adam's answers (both batches)
### 128 The three pickers' display choices where SPEC and the boards give no value (provisional, D31)

### The long form of CONTEXT.md's "REVIEW" line (What exists)
- Files: `src/features/plan/review.ts`, with its tests in the same folder:
  - `review.items.test.ts`: which items there are.
  - `review.actions.test.ts`: what each action writes.
  - `review.text.test.ts`: board 4's wording, checked character for character against `design/1.2/source/PlanReview.dc.html`.
  - `review.seed.test.ts`: the seed's week 2 → week 3, the five items TASKS 43 names.
  - `review.static.test.ts`.
  - The builders in `review.testutil.ts` build the app's own types, so typecheck proves the inputs fit.
  - `weekPlanning.ts` exports `ExerciseSlot`, `pairByExercise` and `pairSets` for it (chunk 43), so REVIEW matches sets as COPY does.
- `reviewItems({ weekNumber, lastWeek: { sessions, plan }, thisWeek, decisions, exercises?, workouts?, weightUnit? })` → one group per session of last week:
  - Groups come in the order of last week's days. A moved session sits under the day it was done, and each session of a plan row that two weekdays share is its own group (G14).
  - Week 1 gives nothing. Last week is week − 1 only, so a missed week gives nothing (131).
  - Only `completed` sessions count. A session `skipped` as a whole gives nothing (G52), and neither does a `planned` or `in_progress` one.
  - A decision lives on THIS week's plan row of the same slot (`weeksOfSlot`), and a decided key never comes back.
- Per planned head (a warmup is a planned set; a stage row is never a set of its own), in set order, warmups numbered apart:
  - "Skipped" (a skipped log, or a `deleted` change row) or "Not logged" (no log in a completed session). Only where the plan had a weight or a rep target. On a swapped slot the swap item stands for the original's remaining sets instead.
  - A number item: the weight differs as the exercise's unit shows it; reps planned as a number were done differently, or done outside a planned range. AMRAP reps never count. RIR shows only alongside.
  - A type item: the type the workout gave differs from the planned type, or the same stage kind has more drops done than planned. That type is the set's `retyped` row (keyed by the planned set, logged or not), else the log's own kind. A kindless dropset switched to Normal is seen only through its row.
  - The count USE writes: the drops done when some were, else the row's count, else the head log's `pending_stages` count, else 1 (141).
  - A set then skipped or never logged keeps its type item, read from its `retyped` row alone (150 (b)). It comes after the set's "Skipped" / "Not logged" (153), or alone when the plan had no numbers. A set deleted afterwards is "Skipped" only. The same kind with another count, on a set not done, is no item.
  - A log of another exercise on a planned set (the seed's swap shape) is no comparison.
- Per exercise:
  - A set added during the session (a log with no planned set) is an ADDED SET item, with the kind it was given (the drops done, else its `pending_stages` count, else 1).
  - The sets of an exercise outside the plan are one ADDED EXERCISE item, placed after the planned exercise logged last before it.
  - A recorded swap is one SWAPPED item ("for N of M sets").
- Keys come from `itemKey` only: `num:<session>:<planned set>`, `skipped:…`, `type:…`, `added-set:<session>:<exercise>:<position>` (a `w` before a warmup's position), `added-ex:<session>:<exercise>`, `swap:<session>:<program exercise>`. A key never holds a set log id (136).
- `applyReviewAction(item, action, thisWeekPlan, newId?)` → `{ decision, writes }`:
  - Writes are named by the week set's own fields (`update_set`, `insert_set`, `delete_set`), or are a `program_edit` (`add_exercise`, `swap_exercise`) for chunk 45's `planProgramChange`.
  - The set is matched in this week on the planned positions: exercise, then position, warmups to warmups.
  - USE (number): the done weight and reps, a range becoming the number. A set planned AMRAP keeps AMRAP and takes the weight only (137). No match → ADD THIS SET.
  - USE (type): the kind and the stage count. Extra stage rows are removed highest first; missing ones are inserted after the last.
  - ADD THIS SET: appended, with the done numbers and kind.
  - REMOVE THIS SET: this week's matching set, its stages with it.
  - IGNORE: the decision only.
  - A done weight below 0, or 0 reps, is left out of a write (027's checks).
- `reviewItemText(item, { fromWeek, period })` → eyebrow, headline, detail, note and action: board 4's own strings, and the choices of 139 and 153.

### The long form of CONTEXT.md's Offline line: the sync queue's `delete` items (chunk 57)
- Files: `src/features/offline/useSyncQueue.ts`, and `src/lib/db.ts` for the queue item's `sendStarted`, `sessionId` and `parentSetId` (plain fields, no Dexie version bump). Tests:
  - `useSyncQueue.order.test.ts` (41), on a fake that models the server: a stage's foreign key, a head's cascade, the call shape (it throws on any filter but `id`), a reply held in flight or lost. Its IndexedDB writes land on a later tick.
  - `useSession.completeSession.test.tsx`: the finish after a queued delete.
- A queue item is `{ table, operation: 'upsert' | 'delete', payload, createdAt, attempts?, gaveUp?, sendStarted?, sessionId?, parentSetId? }`. A pass reads the queue in `createdAt` order and sends one item at a time; passes run one at a time (single-flight, per page).
- A `delete` item's payload is `{ id }`, and its request is `supabase.from(item.table).delete().eq('id', id)`, nothing else. A delete naming no row is never sent: it throws "queued delete names no row", which counts as a failed attempt.
- Order:
  - Every write waits behind a failed or held earlier write to its own record.
  - An upsert also waits behind its session row, and a stage's upsert behind its head.
  - A head's delete also waits behind its stage logs' writes: the stage deletes that name it as `parentSetId`, and the stage upserts that name it as `parent_set_id`.
  - Writes to any other record go.
- Never sent: an upsert with no `sendStarted` and no `attempts`. At the start of each pass, a record whose writes before its first delete are all never-sent upserts loses them and that delete. They are removed in queue order, upsert first, and nothing is sent for them. A write that may be on the server keeps its delete, which goes after it.
- `sendStarted` is written to IndexedDB, awaited, just before an upsert's first request. If that write fails, nothing is sent and it counts as a failed attempt. `retrySyncFailures` resets a write that gave up and marks it `sendStarted`.
- After 5 failed passes a write, a delete too, stops retrying (`gaveUp`). It stays queued, holds back what waits behind it, and is reported with those writes; a delete is reported under the session beside it.
- `hasQueuedWritesFor(sessionId)` also counts a queued delete of that session, so an online finish that still has one queues behind it instead of deriving its status from the server's logs.
- `queueSetLogDelete({ id, sessionId, parentSetId })` queues one delete, then removes the device's own `set_logs` copy; a failed queue write leaves the copy. Producers (61, 63) call it once per log, offline only, stages first and the head last; the screen's cache is theirs to update. Nothing calls it yet.
- Kept as before, for 61, 63 and 64 to know:
  - A queued finish isn't held behind its session's failed log writes (DECISIONS 114: "other records still go"). So one replayed while its session's delete fails again counts the deleted set.
  - Single-flight is per page: two tabs share IndexedDB but not the pass lock.

### From RULES.md, before the display follow-up's review 2 (two lines updated in place; both rules stand)
- **Tailwind v4 builds the stylesheet from every file git doesn't ignore — tests, scripts and the docs included** (chunk 37; the docs: chunk 38, reproduced): the word `'sepia'` in a script test put `.sepia{filter:…}` in the production stylesheet, and since #98 this rule's own quote of it does the same: every build since is `index-rvbY4UeW.css` (`index-BwLO1svn.css` with the word gone from every tracked file). After a chunk that adds no UI (tests, scripts, an unused component), the build's stylesheet name equals staging's deployed one, `index-rvbY4UeW.css` since chunk 38 (#99). A docs edit that adds or removes a bare utility name changes the next build's stylesheet: build after editing the docs and compare the name. Numbered ids are utilities too (chunk 43; reproduced in its review): two fixture ids made of `ps` or `pe` (padding-inline start / end), a hyphen and a number built `index-B0sNRcsx.css`; give a fixture id a shape no utility has (and never quote such an id in a tracked file, this one included).

- **A tracked file that quotes a theme variable by its full name puts that variable in the built stylesheet** (the display follow-up's builder; reproduced in its review). On that branch `global.css`'s `@theme inline` maps `--on-accent` to a Tailwind name. A scratch file holding a regex for that name, written out whole, built a stylesheet with the mapping added to its theme layer: `index-B0SnMOUK.css`, where the tree alone builds `index-ra14cXRp.css`. A test id shaped like a utility does the same (the Tailwind rule above). A test or a doc that must name such a variable builds the name from parts, and a UI chunk's stylesheet is compared with staging's deployed one character by character, not only by name.

### From DECISIONS.md: 151, in full, with Adam's answer
### 151 UNLOG of a set that isn't the last one logged: what happens to the set numbers (chunk 46)
**Ask:** During a workout a logged set can be unlogged (SPEC 18c). Its log is deleted, and its weight, reps and RIR stay on the phone as a draft. A logged set shows the number it was logged with, and an open set shows the next number after the logged ones. So unlogging a set that isn't the last one logged leaves a hole in the logged numbers, and two rows show the same number. With bench 01–03 logged and 04 open, UNLOG on 02 shows 01 ✓, 03 (the unlogged set, open), 03 ✓, 04. The finish warning then says "Bench 03 and 04", and the lock asks "Log set 04 before set 03?". Logging it again stores a second set 3, so History shows sets 1, 3 and 3. SPEC 18c says only that the set "goes back to unlogged with its numbers kept" and that "logging again undoes it". What should unlog do to the set numbers?
**Recommendation:** (a), the rule that a delete (18b) and a switch to or from Warmup (146 (a)) already follow. The logged sets after it close the gap at once, and logging it again gives it the next number. No two rows or logs then share a number, and History has no hole. The set's own number can change: unlog 02 of 01–03 and log it again, and it is 03 (the old 03 became 02). Chunk 46 returns the number patches with the unlog (heads and their drops). Chunk 63 writes them with the delete, offline too, as chunk 61 does for delete.
**Blocks:** chunk 46's merge, and so 58a, 58b and 59–64, which draw from it and write what it returns; 63 writes the answer. As built, after its own unlog the module's own rows show two sets with one number, and every option but (c) changes the module. Nothing before 58a waits: 47–57 don't use it.
**Options:**
- (a) As recommended: the logged sets after it move down one; logging it again gives it the next number.
- (b) The set keeps its number. The draft also keeps the number it was logged with, the open row shows it, and LOG writes it again, so logging again restores exactly what was there. The other sets don't move. A set logged while it is unlogged takes the number after the highest one in use. If it is still unlogged when the session ends, its number is missing in History.
- (c) As built: nothing renumbers. While the set is unlogged two rows show one number, and logging it again stores a duplicate number. Not recommended.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-16) "not (a). An unlogged set keeps its number and its place. Logging it again stores it with that same number, so unlog then log is an exact undo (SPEC 18c). No other set's number changes on unlog. The open row shows its own number (a planned set's position; an added set's number from its draft), never "the next after the logged ones"."
**Evidence:** Executed through the module's own outputs in chunk 46's second review, on `5b09cec` squashed onto staging `4e7205b`:
- `unlogEffects` on 02 returns the log's delete and the draft, nothing else.
- Applied, `resolveRows` reads `01✓ 03· 03✓ 04·`, and the current set is the unlogged 02, shown as 03.
- Logged again the way chunk 58a keeps writing a head (`totalLoggedHeads + 1`; TASKS 58a, "Writes unchanged"), the stored numbers are 1, 3, 3.
- Unlogging the last logged set leaves no hole.

Why SPEC doesn't settle it:
- SPEC 18b's "The remaining sets renumber" is about delete.
- 146 (a) answered the Warmup switch only (RULES.md: an answer covers the cases its question held).
- G46's draft (TASKS 63) holds weight, reps, RIR, form and unit, and no set number.

It is the defect 146 was asked about (two rows with one number), here for unlog. The builder raised it (its report, A8) and built nothing for it. Redone if the answer is (b): the draft's shape and how the rows number a set with a draft (46), and what LOG writes (63).

### 149 Weeks a week-dependent run changed in 1.1's week view, and 143's copy (chunk 45)
**Ask:** In 1.1 the week view was where a week-dependent run's exercises changed. SWAP or ADD made a "week-only" exercise in that week, REMOVE took one out of that week, and the next week copied the week as it was, so the change carried on. The run's program (its copy) never changed: the program tab went in 1.1, and "Make this week the new default" is for stable runs only. 1.2 has no exercise actions in the week view: exercises change only in CHANGE THE PROGRAM, which edits the program. Your answer to 143 makes a copied week follow the program's list. When 044 brings that rule in (chunk 53 on staging; production at the release), what should the first copy from a week like that take?
**Recommendation:** (c): once, at the release, make each active week-dependent run's program match its last planned week (each workout's latest planned normal week, the one its next week is copied from). A week-only exercise joins the program, an exercise that week doesn't have leaves it (soft-removed, as everywhere), and the program takes that week's order. Your next week then looks exactly as 1.1 would have made it, and CHANGE THE PROGRAM shows what you are actually doing, so from then on every exercise can be swapped, removed or reordered. Under (a) or (b) the first 1.2 week of such a run changes by itself.
**Blocks:** chunk 53 (044 runs the copy rule; under (b) its twin changes with it; under (c) chunk 53 or the release plan carries the one-time step) and the release. Not chunks 47–52: none of them runs the copy rule, and no option changes what a CHANGE THE PROGRAM save writes. Staging has no such week (the seed plans every week with `v2_plan_week`), so only production's runs are affected: yours and your friend's, if a week-dependent run changed exercises during 1.1.
**Options:**
- (a) As built (chunk 45's copy rule, which 044 will follow): the program's list and order. An exercise removed in 1.1 for that week comes back with no sets. A week-only exercise stays after the program's exercises, with its sets, and stays in every later week: nothing in 1.2 lists it, so it can never be removed.
- (b) The program's list only: a week-only exercise isn't copied (its sets stay in the weeks that have them), and an exercise removed in 1.1 for that week comes back with no sets. Every exercise of a later week can then be changed in CHANGE THE PROGRAM; a week-only exercise you still want is added there once, with no sets.
- (c) As recommended: once, at the release, the program is made to match the last planned week. It changes existing rows on production (the run copies' `v2_program_exercises`: `week_only`, `removed_at`, `position`), so it runs with live counts before and after, like any migration that changes data. On a sequence run whose repeated workout differs between its slots, one slot's week (the last) decides.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-16) "(c), as a release step, not during the build. One data migration at the release makes each active week-dependent run's program match its last planned week (exercises and order), so nothing the user sees changes. It touches existing rows, so: it's written and tested in chunk 53's scope as its own migration file, rehearsed on staging against a seeded 1.1-shaped run (add that shape to the seed if missing), with before/after counts and a fingerprint, and listed under "For the release" as a blocking decision with the manual backup before it. Chunk 53 is unblocked on that basis."
**Evidence:** What 1.1 stored: the week view's SWAP and ADD call `createWeekOnlyProgramExercise` (`week_only = true`, `runProgramExercises.ts`), and REMOVE deletes the week's rows. 041's week branch copies the source week's own rows (SPEC [P1.1]: "copying uses each week's actual content"). The program tab was removed in 1.1 (DECISIONS 108), and 040's header says "Week-dependent programs don't have this action". CHANGE THE PROGRAM's draft (`draftFromRunCopy`) lists only the program's live rows, and a draft that names a week-only row is refused. The reviewer's executed probe (chunk 45's second review): a Pull whose done week 2 had a 1.1 swap (Lat Pulldown → week-only Machine Row), a removal (Face Pull) and an add (week-only Curl), and no save since. As built, week 3 gets Lat Pulldown ×0, Face Pull ×0, Seated Row ×2, Machine Row ×2, Curl ×1; 041 today gives Seated Row ×2, Machine Row ×2, Curl ×1. After a save that removes Lat Pulldown and Face Pull, the two week-only rows are still copied. Two of SPEC's sentences meet here: 143's "a copied week follows the run copy's current exercise list and order" and [P1.1]'s "copying uses each week's actual content". The builder raised it (its report, 3.B) and kept week-only rows under [P1.1]; the review found that nothing in 1.2 can remove them. Cost: (a) nothing; (b) a few lines of `copyFromWeek` and their tests, in chunk 53 with 044; (c) a one-time data step at the release (designed in chunk 53), with live counts.

### From DECISIONS.md: 152, in full, with Adam's answer
### 152 A warmup logged with no weight or reps, made a working set during the workout (chunk 46, for 62)
**Ask:** SPEC lets a warmup be logged with no weight and no reps (Warmup sets: "weight and reps, both optional"). Its boxes may be left empty, and a warmup ticked off in the tick list has none. A logged set's type can be changed from its edit panel (SPEC 19; board W2b's EDITING A WARMUP has a SET TYPE row). The database refuses a working set without both numbers (`v2_set_logs_check`: `is_skipped or is_warmup or (weight is not null and reps is not null)`). So making such a warmup Normal, or a staged set, fails. What should happen?
**Recommendation:** (a), ask for the numbers first. A working type on such a warmup is saved together with the weight and reps typed in its edit panel, in one write. If a box is empty, SAVE says "Enter weight and reps." and sends nothing. Nothing is refused and nothing done is lost.
**Blocks:** chunk 62 (SET TYPE on a logged set). It blocks chunk 46's merge only under (c). Under (a), (b) and (d), the type patch chunk 46 returns stands: 62 sends the numbers with it, or doesn't offer the pick. Under (c), `applySetTypeChange` returns a delete for such a warmup instead of a patch.
**Options:**
- (a) As recommended: the numbers first, saved with the type in one write.
- (b) Not offered: for a logged warmup with no weight or reps, SET TYPE offers Warmup only (as G55 limits Plan's picker) until its numbers are saved.
- (c) The switch makes it a set still to do. Its warmup log is deleted (it holds nothing), and the set becomes an open working set of the picked type (its `retyped` row), current or upcoming like any open set.
- (d) As built: the write is refused and the error shows; the set stays a warmup.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-16) "(a). Making a numberless logged warmup a working set asks for weight and reps in the panel first; type and numbers are saved in one write."
**Evidence:** Executed on a replay of migrations 000–042 (`supabase/postgres:17.6.1.155`), rolled back:
- A warmup was logged with weight and reps null, as `SetRow.tsx` writes an empty box ("an empty field is simply null").
- The patch chunk 46 returns for Normal (`is_warmup false, stage_kind null`) was refused: `23514 v2_set_logs_check`. The patch for Dropset was refused the same way.
- The control, a warmup logged 20 × 12, was accepted.
- The builder's walk, replayed on the real tables with warmups logged without numbers: 35 of 2230 writes refused, all by this check. With numbers, none of 4334.

Chunk 46's rules read no weight or reps, and their stand-in doesn't model this check, so their own tests can't see it. TASKS 62 patches `is_warmup`, `stage_kind` and `stage_index` only. The builder raised it (its report, A9).

  - Digits only, at most three, with the number pad.
  - The number is selected when a box takes focus, and Enter leaves the box.

  - Escape in a box closes the sheet, as it does anywhere in it.

- (a) as described, or the set's own number carried into its other segment (12 → 12–14), as the first attempt had it;

### 170 An unlogged added set's place after an earlier set is deleted or switched to or from Warmup (chunk 46)
**Ask:** Chunk 46's fourth attempt builds your 161 (b)(i) right. To fix another unlog case, it made an unlogged added set take the number its draft holds, and that breaks the order of the added sets after an edit of an earlier set. DELETE 02, or make it a Warmup: SPEC 18b and your 146 (a) say the sets after it close the gap, so A 03 and B 04. The fourth attempt gives B 03 and A 04: the empty new set jumps ahead of the unlogged one. Two unlogged added sets trade places the same way, also when a Warmup before them is made Normal. The third attempt got all four cases right. It is a behaviour bug, and your rule for this attempt was no retry. Allow a fifth attempt?
**Recommendation:** (a): a fifth attempt in which every writer that moves the numbers also moves the places the phone keeps for its open added sets. Both 151's unlog and 18b's delete then hold. Nothing uses chunk 46 before 58a, so nothing else waits.
**Blocks:** chunk 46's merge, and so 58a, 58b and 59–64, which draw from it. Nothing before 58a.
**Options:**
- (a) A fifth attempt of 46. DELETE and a switch to or from Warmup also give each open added set after the set its new place (its draft's position, or a place the card keeps for a new set), as they give the logged sets their new numbers; chunks 61 and 62 write it. Its walk checks each set by identity, and their order, after every delete and switch. The builder's readings 3 and 4 (Evidence) get the same fix. Recommended.
- (b) Merge as built: after a delete or a Warmup switch before an unlogged added set, a later open added set can take its place. "The sets after it close the gap" then holds for logged sets only.
- (c) Go back to the third attempt's numbering for unlogged added sets (the lowest free number, in their drafts' order, before the new sets). 18b holds, but an added set unlogged while new sets are open before it moves to the front of them, against 151's "no other set's number changes on unlog" (the builder executed this on the third attempt).
**Answer:**
**Evidence:** executed in the review on `9a08d7a`. Each step is the module's own answer, applied as the card and the sync queue will apply it (`<scratchpad>/build/chunk-46-review-4.md`). Bench `n n n`, 01–03 logged, two sets added:
- D: A logged as 04 and unlogged, B new (05); DELETE 02 → B 03, A 04 (the third attempt: A 03, B 04).
- W: the same, with 02 made a Warmup → B 03, A 04 (the third: A 03, B 04).
- 2D: A (04) and C (05) logged and unlogged; DELETE 02 → C 03, A 04 (the third: A 03, C 04).
- MR: bench `w n n`, 01–02 logged; A (03) and C (04) logged and unlogged; the open planned Warmup made Normal → C 04, A 05 (the third: A 04, C 05).
- Cause: new in the fourth attempt, a draft takes its stored position whenever that number is free and no more than the count of working sets. A delete or switch before it leaves the position one too high, and another open added set takes the number the delete gives the draft. Chunk 46's third review accepted out-of-date drafts on the condition that "the row then takes the number 18b's renumbering gives it".
- The walk checks "nothing moves" set by set on unlog only. After a delete or a switch it checks that the numbers read 1 to n, which a swapped order satisfies.
- The builder's readings 3 and 4 have the same root (by reading, not executed). A never-logged added Warmup with a logged added set after it, made Normal again, joins after that set (146 (a): "takes its place"). Two added Warmups holding one stored number can swap W1 and W2 on an unlog (161: "nothing moves").
- Everything else is right. 161 (b)(i), executed: an added Warmup and an added Dropset ×1 unlogged come back as they were, nothing moves, and logging again restores them. Review 3's case: an open added Warmup is not the current set, and the lock answers `log` for it. ### Adam's answers of 2026-10-19, second batch, word for word
- 173: (a), a sixth attempt of chunk 46, Opus builder, with:
  - Warmups follow the same numbering rule as working sets: when a warmup's displayed number changes (delete, switch to or from Warmup), its log's stored number is patched, so a log never keeps a number its row no longer shows.

### 173 Chunk 46's fifth attempt: a warmup log's number, and a set added in a reopened session (chunk 46)
**Ask:** Chunk 46's fifth attempt builds your 170 right for the working sets, and your named break fails its sequence test. Two behaviour bugs remain. Allow a sixth attempt that fixes both?
- (1) A warmup's log keeps a number it no longer shows.
  - A logged set made a Warmup keeps its working number: logged as 04, it shows W1 and still holds 4. A logged warmup keeps its W number when a set before it is switched or deleted.
  - So unlog then log stores another number (4 → 1).
  - Two added sets, logged and then both made Warmups, hold the same number. REVIEW then shows one item, "warmup 04", for the two.
  - SPEC 18b says "LOG stores the number the row shows; a delete or a switch … that changes logged sets' numbers patches them". That, and 18c's exact undo, cover warmups too, and 1.1 stores a warmup's W number.
- (2) A set added while the card's list doesn't name the earlier added sets is drawn before them. That happens in a session reopened with CONTINUE SESSION, or on another phone.
  - Example: bench 01–03 and two added sets logged as 04 and 05. Reopened, + ADD SET: the new set shows 04, and the two older ones 05 and 06, while their logs still hold 4 and 5.
  - Logging the new set stores a second 4, and REVIEW shows two items for the three added sets.
  - 170 says "added sets by when they were added".

**Recommendation:** (a). Both fixes are small and in 46.
- The renumbering also gives each logged warmup its W number.
- Any added set the card's list doesn't name is taken into the list before a new set is added, so a new set always comes last.
- The sequence test then checks warmups' stored numbers and the exact undo in full, and adds reload and reopen steps.
- Nothing uses 46 before 58a.

### 174, full text as the builder worded it (`chunk-46-builder-6.md`, section 3), before Adam's answer
**Ask:** 173's second bullet keeps an added set's place "from its log once logged" across a reopen. After 173's first bullet, a warmup's log holds its W number, and then no column of `v2_set_logs` says where an added Warmup stands among the working added sets (executed: two histories store the same rows and need opposite orders). Add a column for the place, or take one of the other options?

**Recommendation:** (a). It is one nullable column with no default, add-only (D29), and it says plainly what it holds.

**Blocks:** chunk 46 (its sixth attempt stopped before building), so 58a–64. Nothing before 58a.

**Options:**
- **(a) A column.** `v2_set_logs.added_place integer null` (no default), holding the set's place among the sets added to its exercise in the session, from 1, in the order they were added.
  - It is null on a planned set's log, on a drop, and on every log written before 1.2. 1.1 added working sets only, numbered as logged, so a null place is ordered by `set_number`, before the placed ones.
  - An optional `check (added_place is null or added_place >= 1)` would be flagged by `check-migration` as 042's checks were, and logged under "For the release".
  - Written by:
    - ADD SET / ADD ROUND (58a): the new list entry gets 1 + the highest place the card knows (its list, the session's logs of that exercise, its drafts). On one phone a set added in a reopened session therefore comes after every set added earlier. Two phones adding at once can tie; the log's id breaks the tie.
    - LOG of an added set (58a): writes the entry's place.
    - The skips that log an added set (59's "skip the rest of this exercise", 61's SKIP THIS SET): write the place.
    - Unlog (63): the draft and the Dexie list entry keep the place. Re-LOG (63) writes it again.
    - A type change (62) and DELETE (61) leave it alone.
  - Read by 46 only. The module orders every added set by place, then id, wherever its place comes from: the list entry, the log, or a draft no listed set has. REVIEW, History and Coach don't need it (`select *` returns the extra column; named lists are unaffected).
  - Plumbing (a migration chunk, like 47):
    - `SetLog.addedPlace` and the mappers (`toSetLog`, the Dexie `set_logs` cache);
    - the LOG upsert payload in `useSession.ts`. A payload naming the column fails until the migration is live, so the migration goes live before 58a (RULES: a named column joins a list only once its migration is live). 58a's R4 parity payload for a planned set stays as it is if the column is left out of it.
    - `probe-live-columns` gets a spec for the column.
  - Number and order: CONTEXT's next number is 044, planned for 53's `v2_plan_week`, and 53 also numbers 149's data migration. The build order has 53 before 58a, so this migration is the next free number at the time.
  - TASKS lines that change: the Data model (a row for the place), the Migration summary, the Process notes' migration list, 46, 58a, 59, 61, 63, and CONTEXT's next-migration line. A timestamp `added_at` is the variant: it needs no counting, but a phone's clock can put a new set before older ones.
- **(b) No migration: the log's id is the set's own id, made in time order when the set is added** (a UUIDv7-shaped id), and LOG, re-LOG and the skips all write the log with it. The module orders by id.
  - It hides an order in ids nobody can see. An id made the old way (crypto.randomUUID(), 1.1's logs) orders arbitrarily, and two phones' clocks can disagree.
  - It changes TASKS 63, whose re-log is "a new log row … (new id)".
  - The sync queue already keeps a re-insert after a delete of the same row in order ("a write that fails holds back every later write to that record"), but no test pins that shape. Not recommended.
- **(c) A rule instead of a place, for that one shape.**
  - After a reopen, or on another phone, an added Warmup whose list entry is gone stands where a fixed rule puts it, for example after the working added sets. Made Normal again, it can then land in another place than before the reopen.
  - This relaxes 170's "added sets by when they were added" for that case. The generator's reopen step would re-derive the walk's own record by the same rule: a weaker invariant, which Adam's "the same invariants after every step" doesn't allow without his word.
- **(d) The phone keeps the card's list past the session's end** (TASKS 63, Dexie), so CONTINUE SESSION on the same phone keeps the order.
  - Another phone, or a cleared cache, has no list, and there the probe's H2 is drawn wrong.
  - It doesn't meet "from its log once logged".

**Evidence:** the probe above, and the column census.

### 177 Do the drop and stage logs of an added set also carry `added_place`? (pre-read, chunk 46)
**Ask:** an added set's place is "written when the added set's log is first written" (174). A staged added set has several logs: its head, and one per drop or stage. Does each drop or stage log hold the place too, or only the head's log?
**Recommendation:** (a), the head's log only. The place belongs to the set. A drop is always drawn under its head (`parentSetId`, `stageIndex`), and a head can't be unlogged while a drop of it is logged (18c), so a drop's copy would never be read.
**Blocks:** chunk 46's sixth attempt (which logs the reader reads the place from, and which logs the null fallback covers); then 58a's payload for a drop or stage LOG.
**Options:**
- (a) Head only: drop and stage logs hold null. 46 reads the place from head logs (`stageIndex` 0) and never from a stage row, and the 46m fallback ("null and no planned set") covers head logs only. TASKS 46m's writer list loses `handleLogStage`.
- (b) Every log of an added set holds its set's place: 58a's `handleLogStage` writes the head's place with each drop or stage. 46 reads it from the head, and a test checks that each drop holds its head's place.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-19) "no. Only an added set's own log carries added_place; its drop and stage logs leave it null."
**Evidence:** Adam's words (174 and the writers' mapping) say "an added set's place" and "the added set's log", as if there were one log. TASKS 46m's writer list names `handleLogStage` among the LOG paths of an added set, which reads as (b). The sixth attempt's plan (`<scratchpad>/build/chunk-46-builder-6.md`, section 3, option (a)) has the place "null … on a drop", which is (a). Chunk 46m's review left it open for this pre-read (carry notes). A drop log has `weekPlanSetId` null too, so under (a) the reader must not take it for a pre-044 log. What is redone if the answer goes the other way: 58a's stage payload, and one reader test in 46.

### 178 An added set left unlogged when the session ends: what patches the logged sets after it? (pre-read, chunk 46)
**Ask:** an added set with no log exists only in the card's list and its draft, and both end with the session (G46; TASKS 63: "the session's end clears the session's drafts"; 174 didn't keep the list past the session). Once it is gone, each logged set after it shows a number one lower than its log holds, and the next set added stores a number that a log already holds. What writes their new numbers?
- Example, with the lock on: Bench 01–03 logged; A and B added and logged as 04 and 05; A unlogged; FINISH, COMPLETE; CONTINUE SESSION. The rows read 01✓ 02✓ 03✓ B✓, with B shown as 04 and its log holding 5. + ADD SET gives N, shown as 05, and LOG stores 5. Two logs hold 5.
- The same happens on another phone during the session (it never had A's draft), and with the lock off, A never logged.
**Recommendation:** (b). The module reports each logged set whose stored number isn't the number its row shows, and the card writes those patches when it draws the rows (after a reopen, after a reload without the drafts, on another phone), queued offline like a delete's. It is the only option that keeps 173's "no two logs ever hold one number" on every phone. Its cost: with two phones open at once and a draft on one of them, each phone patches the numbers back to its own view when it refetches.
**Blocks:** chunk 46's sixth attempt. 173's reopen step, checked with stored = shown and "no two logs share a number", fails on this shape once the warmup carve-outs come out.
**Options:**
- (a) The session's end counts an unlogged added set as deleted: FINISH (64, and auto-finish) writes the renumber that `deleteEffects` gives for it before the session completes. That covers a reopen. Another phone during the session can still show a stale number and store a duplicate.
- (b) A reconcile when the rows are drawn (recommended): from 46's module, written by the card (58a).
- (c) FINISH logs each unlogged added set as skipped, so it keeps its place and number after a reopen. That is a skipped row the user never asked for (REVIEW lists no skipped added set).
- (d) Accept it: after a reopen or on another phone, a logged set may show a number its log doesn't hold, and two logs can hold one number. That relaxes 173.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-19) "(a), with limits. Chunk 46's rules report the logged sets whose stored number differs from the number their row shows; the workout screen writes the corrected numbers when it draws the session's rows. It writes only where they differ, so drawing the same session again writes nothing. It writes only from the workout screen for an in-progress or reopened session, never from History, Plan or any read-only view. Offline, the writes queue like a delete's. Tests: a session ended with an unlogged added set, reopened, gets one correction write; a second draw gets none (break-proven both ways)."
**Evidence:** SPEC 18b (170) names two things that patch stored numbers, a delete and a switch to or from Warmup; a set that leaves with the session's end is neither. Review 5's F2 is this shape with every added set logged, which 044's place fixes. With one of them unlogged at the end, the place keeps the order, but the number of each set after it still moves. Read, not executed (a read-only pre-read): from the rank rule at `d09a241` (`workoutRules.ts`, its header's "What a row's number is") and 170.

### 179 The sets a swap for today moves: added sets with a place, or none? (pre-read, chunk 46)
**Ask:** a swap for today moves the original's open sets to the new exercise with their numbers, type, drops and targets (164), and they are logged with no planned set. That makes them sets of the new exercise that no plan holds, as an added set is. But TASKS 46m's writer list says only 58a's + ADD SET / + ADD ROUND and 59's "Add a set" create an added set, so nothing gives the moved sets a place. Do they get one?
**Recommendation:** (a), yes. The swap creates them as added sets of the new exercise, each given its place by 46's rule in the order they stood (1, 2, …), and 59 writes the place with each moved set's log, as for any added set. Without one, their logs fall into the pre-044 fallback (logged time, then id), and a moved set made a Warmup brings back 174's shape: after a reopen, nothing says where it stood among the moved working sets.
**Blocks:** chunk 46's sixth attempt, whose module has no input for a moved set (164's Blocks said so) and whose order and `nextAddedPlace` must take them in; then 59.
**Options:**
- (a) Added sets with a place (recommended): in the card's list (`OrderExercise.added`) with their types (161), ranked after the original's logged sets so they keep their numbers (164: "03 after 01–02"). 59 assigns and writes the place, and TASKS 46m's mapping gains the swap.
- (b) Not added sets: their logs leave `added_place` null, and the module orders a swapped card's sets that have no planned set and no place by their number, before its placed added sets. There is no new writer, but the null fallback then covers logs written after 044 too, and a moved Warmup's order is lost on a reopen (above).
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-19) "yes. Sets moved by a swap for today count as added sets of the new exercise. Each gets its place at the swap, in their order, after any sets already added to that exercise; chunk 59 writes it."

### 175 Chunk 51b's display choices on CHANGE THE PROGRAM's DAYS card and set rows (provisional, D31)
**Ask:** chunk 51b built the DAYS card and a stable run's set rows with these display choices, which no board or SPEC sentence settles, or where the screen differs from a board's drawing. Accept them, or change any?
**Recommendation:** accept all: each is display only and changes nothing that is written. (b) changes 51a's chips on weekday runs and (l) is the contract 54b sends, so they are the ones to look at.
**Blocks:** nothing.
**Options:** accept as built, or change any of:
- (a) RENAME is in the DAYS card's header (PL1) on a weekday run; a sequence run, which has no card, keeps 51a's row under the chips (172 (a), now for sequence runs only).
- (b) The workout chips show the draft's days, as PL1 draws Pull 1 on WED beside "Was Tuesday"; 51a drew the days in force that week (172 (a)), which this replaces on weekday runs. The card's struck-through day and its "Was …" line say what this week has.
- (c) The taken-day lines ("Sat is Arms's day") are always shown, not only when tapped: a disabled day can't be tapped.
- (d) A workout that never had a day (a spare one) may be given days and lose them again, as `planSchedule` has it; "had a day" is read from the run copy's schedule, the one the edit starts from.
- (e) A new stage has no rep target of its own (as the planner's `addProgramSetStage`).
- (f) The kind label goes under the rep target when the two don't fit side by side (the box is about 115 px wide at 375) and ends in an ellipsis only at 360 px with `REST-PAUSE · 10`; the REST AFTER column is the board's 128 px and gives up to 32 px to the rep box on a narrower screen.
- (g) "NO SETS YET", drawn in `--error`, on a stable card with no set (an exercise just added), and no ALL row until it has one.
- (h) Warmups: the row says `W` (`AW` in a superset), numbered apart from the working sets (SPEC 18b, DECISIONS 170); a picker's eyebrow says the number among the working sets, or among the warmups for a warmup.
- (i) ALL sets every set, a warmup too; its picker opens with one set, so "Use for all" isn't offered, and its eyebrow says `SET 01` (chunk 39's picker has no eyebrow for "all sets").

**Ask:** your 155 (a) is built (d31b, #162): a picker switched to a segment the set doesn't have carries the set's own value over (NUMBER n → RANGE n–(n+2), RANGE a–b → NUMBER a), and the boards' examples start a segment only when the set has no target at all. - (b) **"The set's own value" is the target the sheet opened with.** A number stepped or typed in the set's own segment before the switch isn't carried: 12 stepped to 13, then RANGE, gives 12–14 (and NUMBER again gives 13); 6–9 with FROM typed 5, then NUMBER, gives 6 (and RANGE again gives 5–9).

Nothing is written that the user hasn't seen in the boxes and on the footer before SET, and each is a few lines in `pickerLogic.ts` to change.

- (b) as built, or carry what the box shows at the tap (13 → RANGE 13–15), with a mark per segment so that 6–9 → NUMBER → RANGE still gives 6–9.

### 184 A set added before 1.2, unlogged and logged again under 1.2: it can't come back in its place (for 63, and 46's redraw)
**Ask:** an added set logged before migration 044 has no place, so its order is the time it was logged (your 174). Unlogged under 1.2, its draft has neither a place nor a time, and logged again it gets a new time. With three added sets 02, 03 and 04 all logged before 1.2, UNLOG 03 draws the old 04 as 03 and the unlogged set as 04; LOG again stores 4, and the old 04 is then corrected to 3. Your 151 says an unlog moves nothing and unlog then log is an exact undo. What should happen?
**Recommendation:** (b). The unlog then moves nothing (151), and only the re-log moves the set, to after the other sets added before 1.2. It needs a session holding sets added before 1.2 (the one in progress at the release, or one reopened later) and an unlog of one that isn't the last; numbers stay 1 to n with no number twice whichever option, so the exact undo isn't worth writing an old time into a new log.

**Options:**
- (a) Exact: the draft keeps the log's time and is drawn in its place (46), and the re-log writes that time back as the new log's `logged_at` (63). The set then reads as logged at its first time, and the newest log's time is what auto-finish and the session's end time read (`useAutoFinishSession.ts`, `sessionCompletion.ts`): a re-log wouldn't count as the session's latest activity.
- (b) The draft keeps the log's time, so the unlog moves nothing (46); the re-log writes the time it happens, so the set moves to after the other old added sets then (recommended).
- (c) As built: the unlog draws it after the other old added sets, and the re-log keeps it there.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-20) "(b). The unlog moves nothing; the re-log may." Option (b), as the entry words it: "The draft keeps the log's time, so the unlog moves nothing (46); the re-log writes the time it happens, so the set moves to after the other old added sets then (recommended)."

### 185 Two phones on one session: 178's corrections go back and forth (for 58a)
**Ask:** the workout screen writes a logged set's shown number over its stored one where they differ (your 178). A set added and not logged yet exists only on the phone that added it (G46). Meanwhile a set the other phone logs can take the number the first phone just wrote, so two logs hold one number. What should 58a write?
**Recommendation:** (c). The phone that holds the open set is the only one that knows it is there, so it leaves the numbers after it alone; the other phone corrects them once; when the set is logged (both phones then see it) or deleted, both agree and nothing more is written.
**Blocks:** 58a.
**Options:**
- (a) As built: accept the back-and-forth, the cost your 178's recommended option named.
- (b) Correct only on the first draw after the session is opened, reopened or reloaded. Fewer writes, but a phone that later logs the open set keeps a number another log holds until its next reload.
- (c) Never correct a log that comes after an open added set on its card (recommended); every other correction as 178 says.
- (d) Keep a set added and not logged yet on the server, so every phone sees it. That changes G46 ("not on the server") and needs a migration.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-20) "(c). A phone never corrects a stored number after a set only it holds." Option (c), as the entry words it: "Never correct a log that comes after an open added set on its card (recommended); every other correction as 178 says."

### 188 A week deload mark that stops part way leaves the week half marked, and marking it again loses a session's saved plan (older than 1.2; found in chunk 52's review)
**Ask:** a week mark with the Settings rules on is one request sequence per session, in turn. If it stops part way (the connection drops, the app is closed), the week is half marked, WEEK ⋯ offers MARK WEEK AS DELOAD again (not every session is marked), and pressing it saves a marked session's deloaded sets over its saved plan, so UNMARK later brings the deload back, not the plan. Fix it in 1.2, and how?
**Recommendation:** (a): `markSessionDeload` leaves a session that already holds a saved pre-deload copy as it is (its flag set, nothing recalculated or saved again), so marking a half-marked week again only finishes the mark. A small behaviour fix with a test of the sequence below, in its own small chunk before the release or inside 54a, which edits Plan; it changes no stored row.
**Blocks:** nothing: it is in production since phase 1 (chunks 21–22), and on staging the same way.
**Options:**
- (a) the guard in `markSessionDeload`, as recommended;
- (b) the week mark as one all-or-nothing request: `v2_apply_ops` can't do it as built (on `v2_week_plans` it updates `deload_restore` only, 142), so this needs 043's function changed and a migration;
- (c) leave it: it needs a mark cut off part way and a second press.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-20) "(a). markSessionDeload leaves a session that already holds a saved copy as it is. Its own small chunk before the release, with a test for the interrupted-then-repeated mark; not inside 54a." Option (a), as the entry words it: "the guard in `markSessionDeload`, as recommended", the recommendation being: "`markSessionDeload` leaves a session that already holds a saved pre-deload copy as it is (its flag set, nothing recalculated or saved again), so marking a half-marked week again only finishes the mark. A small behaviour fix with a test of the sequence below … it changes no stored row." Queued as chunk 188f (TASKS-1.2).
**Evidence:** chunk 52's second review. On staging the reviewer's tool closed the page 3.5 s into a WEEK ⋯ mark of the test account's week 4 (three sessions not started, the Settings rules on): Upper B was marked with its saved copy, Upper A flagged with its saved copy and its sets not yet rewritten, Lower A untouched. Probe B, executed (the real PlanPage, hook and `weekPlanService.ts` over `fakeDeloadDb`): Push of week 4 marked on its own (4 sets of 100 at RIR 2 became 2 sets at RIR 4, its copy 4 entries); MARK WEEK AS DELOAD from WEEK ⋯ saved Push's copy again from its deloaded sets (2 entries); UNMARK left Push with 2 sets at RIR 4, its plan gone, while Pull came back whole. Read in `weekPlanService.ts`: `markWeekDeload` runs `markSessionDeload` for each session of the week, and `markSessionDeload` doesn't look at an existing `deload_restore`. Staging was put back session by session with the week panel's own DELOAD toggle (`unmarkSessionDeload` restores from the saved copy): week 4's content is again what PLAN FORWARD wrote.

### 191 UNDO on CHANGE THE PROGRAM can put an exercise back inside another superset, and the draft then can't be saved (merged 51a; found by chunk 176's builder)
**Ask:** fix 51a's UNDO so it never splits a superset? And where: its own small fix chunk, or with the tests-owed run?
**Recommendation:** fix it in a small chunk of its own, after 176 (merged). 51a is merged, so the fix is a follow-up. The tests-owed run adds tests only, so a change to `changeProgramDraft.ts` doesn't belong there. The fix: `undoRemove` applies the member rule it already has for a removed superset member (`at <= first ? first : last + 1`) to any exercise whose recorded place falls strictly inside a block's span. Then the guard in the 176 draft walk's `case 'undo'` comes out (its comment names this bug), and both recipes below become page tests.
**Blocks:** nothing in the build. Nothing wrong is ever written: SAVE refuses the draft and sends no request. But the person can't save, and nothing on the screen shows why.
**Options:** (a) the builder's fix above: the exercise lands just before or just after the block, never inside it (recommended); (b) UNDO is refused while a block stands where the exercise was; (c) the exercise goes to the end of the list.
**Answer:** (Adam, 2026-10-20, before this entry was written; TASKS-1.2 "Chunk 51c") "write it up as a small DATA fix chunk, placed before 54a". Chunk 51c builds (a): the member rule for any exercise whose recorded place falls inside a block's span, after 53 and before 54a, and it needs 176 merged. Under the cost rule it is a data chunk: full review, break proofs, and a staging check of CHANGE THE PROGRAM's SAVE.
**Evidence:** `undoRemove` (`src/features/programs/changeProgramDraft.ts`, ~190–203) puts the exercise back at `Math.min(gone.at, length)`. It snaps to the block only when the removed exercise was itself a member. SPEC says nothing on where UNDO puts an exercise back; the code comment says "so the block stays in one piece".

Reproduced in the review on the rebased branch, with the builder's probe (`<scratchpad>/build/c176/probes/zzProbe176.test.tsx`; the review's copy, which writes its lines to a file because this repo's test setup hides console output, is in `<scratchpad>/build/r176/probes/`) run through the real screen and hooks:
- Recipe 1 (Push: Bench Press, Overhead Press, then the Lateral Raise + Triceps Pushdown superset): REMOVE Bench Press, REMOVE Triceps Pushdown, UNDO Bench Press, UNDO Triceps Pushdown. The cards then read Bench Press, Overhead Press, Triceps Pushdown, Lateral Raise, and no SUPERSET header is drawn.
- Recipe 2 (Legs): REMOVE Romanian Deadlift; SUPERSET on Back Squat (it joins the block below); UNDO Romanian Deadlift. The cards read Back Squat, Romanian Deadlift, Leg Curl, Calf Raise.
- In both, SAVE shows "Couldn't save the changes." and then the planner's own message, "workout push: the members of superset block blk-push are not next to each other" (`blk-legs` in recipe 2). No request is sent.
- The control, UNDO in stack order (Triceps Pushdown first), restores the original list.

In general: remove B from A, B, C, D; link A with C; UNDO B. Also, unpinned: UNDO of a trio's middle member brings it back last in its block, which the code comment allows.

### 207 Past weeks keep their change marks, compared as they are now: a stable run's done week can be marked against a default changed later (chunk 54b)
**Ask:** should a stable run's past week, or a session that is done, still show change marks compared with the default as it is today?
**Recommendation:** (b). A week-dependent past week is compared with the week before it, and both are locked, so its marks stay true. A stable run's done week is compared with today's default. Its marks can say the week lost or gained what only the default changed, which contradicts "show what was planned".
**Blocks:** nothing (display only; nothing is written either way).
**Options:**
- (a) Keep as built (1.1's G22, SPEC's "anything in a week that differs from its source"): every open plan is compared as it is now, past weeks and done sessions included.
- (b) A stable run's past week and its finished sessions show no marks and no legend. Week-dependent ones keep theirs. This is one condition in `WeekView.tsx`.
- (c) No marks on any past week or finished session.
**Answer:**
**Evidence:** chunk 51b's second review saw this on staging. After a real CHANGE THE PROGRAM save that gave EZ-Bar Curl's default a third set, the stable account's done week 1 Saturday drew a removed-set row "03 | 10–12" that the week never had (its rows and logs were unchanged). Since 54b, week 1 is compared with nothing, so that row no longer appears. The same thing can still happen from week 2 on.
- SPEC: "Done sessions and finished weeks are locked in Plan and show what was planned"; "Stable: set counts, kinds, stages and rep targets compared with the default". SPEC doesn't say whether the default is the one as it was then or as it is now.
- Boards: 11 draws the legend on a done session of a week-dependent week; 1c is week 1, where nothing is compared.
- Builder's report, section 3, item 6: the fix for (b) is `changes = null` when the week is past or the session finished and the run is stable.

### 208 A session an UNMARK cut off part way keeps its saved copy and its flag; marking the week again leaves it marked but not deloaded (chunk 188f)
**Ask:** when a session holds a saved copy but its sets are its plan again (an UNMARK cut off after it put the plan back and before it cleared the copy), should a MARK deload it, or leave it as it is?
**Recommendation:** (a), as built. SPEC's words cover the case ("Marking a session that already holds a saved copy of its plan … leaves it as it is"), and nothing is lost or written wrong: the mark writes only the flag, and UNMARK still restores the plan from the copy. The case needs two things to go wrong in a row: an UNMARK cut off between two of its requests, then MARK pressed rather than UNMARK.
**Blocks:** nothing (no data lost or written wrong either way).
**Options:**
- (a) As built: a session that holds a saved copy is left as it is, whatever its sets are. It reads DELOAD with its plan's sets (or with none, when the cut came before the plan went back in) until it is unmarked; UNMARK, then MARK, deloads it.
- (b) A mark first finishes an UNMARK it finds cut off: a session whose sets equal its saved copy, or that holds none, is put back from the copy and then marked as an unmarked session is. One more comparison in `markSessionDeload`, in a production fix's code path.
**Answer:**
**Evidence:** 188's question held a week mark cut off part way (chunk 52's review, probe B), so its answer doesn't settle this case (RULES: "An answer covers the cases its question held"); SPEC's words read literally do.
- UNMARK is three requests (`applyDeloadRestore`): delete the sets, put the copy's sets back, then clear the copy and the flag in one write. Cut after the second, the session holds its flag, its copy and the plan's sets. A week reads marked only when every session is (`weekIsFullyDeload`, `PlanPage.tsx`), so after an UNMARK WEEK cut off there, WEEK ⋯ offers MARK WEEK AS DELOAD.
- The builder executed it (report §3.3, a scratch probe, not committed): after MARK WEEK that session was unchanged (flag on, copy of 4 entries, the plan's 4 × 100 at RIR 2), the other session was deloaded, and UNMARK WEEK put both back.
- Before 188f, the same press deloaded that session correctly. But cut before the second request (no sets), it saved an empty copy over the plan, and every session the UNMARK hadn't reached had its deloaded sets saved over its plan (188). The builder's hook test (3) builds the no-sets state from a cut-off MARK; under the guard's removal (G1) its copy read `[]`.
- Settled, not asked: an empty copy (`[]`, a session marked with no sets of its own) counts as a copy, as `unmarkSessionDeload` reads it. Reading it as none would bring 188 back for such a session, whose calculated sets come from the base week (break G3 fails 2 tests).

### 210 VOLUME's empty last week (P1.2-2): a week with no plan sets and no session, not every week with no session (chunk 55)
**Ask:** P1.2-2 says last week's column shows "—" "when last week has no sessions at all (planned forward from an empty week)". Chunk 55 reads "empty" as 131's week with nothing in it: no plan row of it holds a set and no session of it exists. Should a week that was planned but has no session also show "—"?
**Recommendation:** (a), as built. SPEC 14 and your 133 say what such a week counts (its plan while it runs, 0 once it has ended, with the "YOU PLANNED … DID …" notes), and P1.2-2 is a provisional display choice (TASKS' D31 table), not a SPEC rule; its own parenthetical names the case it was written for, a week planned forward from an empty one.
**Blocks:** nothing (display: nothing is written either way; one line in `lastWeekIsEmpty`, `volumeSheetLogic.ts`, if (b)).
**Options:**
- (a) As built: "—" only for a week with no planned set and no session (a missed week, 131, or one planned with no sets). A planned week with no session shows numbers: its plan on a week planned ahead (Monday morning, nothing started yet), 0 with the notes once it has ended.
- (b) The literal words: "—" for every week with no session row. On a week planned ahead that hides the plan counts SPEC 14 asks for ("sessions not done yet count their plan"), and on a week that ended it hides the "YOU PLANNED 4 LAST WEEK · DID 0" notes your 133 asked for ("so the note shows what was missed").
**Answer:**
**Evidence:** the builder's report, reading 3. Both cases are tested and break-proven: "a planned week nobody did anything in is not empty" (`VolumeSheet.test.tsx`) fails under the literal reading (the review's break R1, `return sessionCount === 0`), and a missed week shows dashes with nothing read (break V13 and the page test). A week whose sessions were all skipped has session rows and counts 0 under either option. SPEC is silent on "—"; SPEC 14 and 133's words decide the numbers (TASKS' D31 table is "built as written unless Adam changes them", provisional by its own header), so this is listed for your review pass, not held as a gap.

### 212 A workout whose session this week is already done gets no REVIEW items (chunk 56; SPEC is silent)
**Ask:** when this week's session of a workout is done (completed or skipped) before last week's differences for it were decided, should REVIEW still offer them? As built it doesn't: Plan leaves a done session's plan row out of what REVIEW reads, so that workout's items go, and the line's count with them; they come back if the session is reopened.
**Recommendation:** (a), as built. A done session is locked in Plan (SPEC: "Done sessions and finished weeks are locked in Plan"; Actions: "Each writes to the week shown"), so USE, ADD THIS SET, REMOVE THIS SET and a type item's USE have nowhere to write. The workout's differences come back one week on, from this week's done session, on next week's REVIEW (a week planned ahead shows them already).
**Blocks:** nothing. Nothing is written for those items either way; (b) or (c) is the filter in `PlanPage.tsx`'s `reviewArgs` plus a per-item one in the sheet.
**Options:**
- (a) As built: no items for a workout whose session this week is done.
- (b) Still offer its ADD EXERCISE and SWAP FROM WEEK N items, which are CHANGE THE PROGRAM changes and land from the next week for that workout (How a save lands leaves a done session as it is); drop its per-set items.
- (c) Offer every item, the per-set ones with IGNORE only.
**Answer:**
**Evidence:** the builder's report, point 1. `reviewArgs.thisWeek` leaves out `doneWeekPlanIds`, and chunk 43's rule "no counterpart this week, nowhere to store a decision or write" then drops the items. Break G1 (done rows passed in) is caught by `PlanPage.review.test.tsx` (re-run in the review). A session in progress isn't locked, so its items stay: staging's week 3 Upper A is in progress, and TASKS 56's five items show there. SPEC's REVIEW section says which week "last week" is, not which of this week's sessions can take its decisions.
